explain: Correct: E, B, C — closed systems, dependent drainage, and front-to-back hygiene prevent bacterial entry. A breaks the closed system. D is done only when ordered, not routinely.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which technique is correct for logrolling a client after spinal surgery?
options: Turn the client as a unit with a pillow between the legs
Twist the client at the waist, at the patient's bedside
Pull the client by the arms, before the end of the shift
Have the client sit up first, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — the spine stays aligned as one unit with leg support. B twists the spine. D flexes it. C strains shoulders and misaligns the spine.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: dopamine 5 mcg/kg/min for a client weighing 70 kg. Available: dopamine 400 mg in 250 mL. What is the rate in mL/hr?
explain: Correct: B — 5 x 70 = 350 mcg/min; 400 mg/250 mL = 1,600 mcg/mL; 350/1,600 = 0.219 mL/min x 60 = 13.1 mL/hr. The other options misconvert milligrams to micrograms or minutes to hours.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medications require an independent double-check by two nurses per most policies? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, E, B — high-alert medications (insulin, heparin, chemo) require independent double-checks. D and C are low-risk routine drugs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which is the antidote for benzodiazepine overdose?
explain: Correct: D — flumazenil reverses benzodiazepines. C reverses opioids. A reverses heparin. B reverses warfarin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client on lithium has coarse hand tremors, confusion, and vomiting. Lithium level is 2.0 mEq/L. What should the nurse do?
options: Hold the lithium, notify the provider, and encourage fluids if not contraindicated
Restrict all fluids, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Give sodium polystyrene sulfonate, in practice
Give the next scheduled dose, using the equipment available at the bedside
explain: Correct: A — a level of 2.0 exceeds the therapeutic 0.6-1.2 range; toxicity needs the drug held, provider notified, and hydration supported. D worsens toxicity. B concentrates lithium further. C treats hyperkalemia, not lithium toxicity.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client receiving vancomycin develops flushing of the face and neck during the infusion. What should the nurse do?
options: Give the next dose as a rapid bolus
explain: Correct: C — red man syndrome comes from rapid vancomycin infusion; slowing it resolves symptoms and the drug can continue. A is unnecessary. D and B worsen the reaction.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which statements about total parenteral nutrition (TPN) are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Use a dedicated central line lumen
Change tubing and filter per protocol
Infuse rapidly to catch up if behind schedule
Stop the infusion abruptly when the bag empties
explain: Correct: A, C, B — TPN needs its own lumen, glucose monitoring for hyperglycemia, and scheduled tubing/filter changes. D is wrong — never catch up; it causes dangerous glucose swings. E is wrong — abrupt stops cause rebound hypoglycemia; hang dextrose if TPN is delayed.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which is the antidote for heparin?
explain: Correct: B — protamine sulfate reverses heparin. C reverses warfarin. D reverses opioids. A reverses benzodiazepines.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes levothyroxine. Which instruction is correct?
options: Take it at bedtime with a snack, and explain the procedure to the patient beforehand
Double the dose if one is missed, during the current shift
Take it with calcium or iron supplements, for now
Take it on an empty stomach in the morning, 30 to 60 minutes before food
explain: Correct: D — food, calcium, and iron impair absorption, so morning dosing on an empty stomach is standard. C blocks absorption. A mistimes the dose. B risks overdose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are expected effects or risks of opioid therapy? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, A — opioids slow the gut (constipation), depress respirations, and cause urinary retention. C is the opposite effect. B is wrong — opioids tend to lower blood pressure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with heart failure takes furosemide and digoxin. Which lab value is most concerning?
explain: Correct: B — hypokalemia from the loop diuretic sharply increases digoxin toxicity risk. C, D, and A are normal values.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: How should the nurse administer ear drops to an adult?
options: Pull the pinna up and back
Tilt the head toward the treated ear
Pull the pinna down and back
explain: Correct: A — up and back straightens the adult ear canal. D is the pediatric technique. B and C do not open the canal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which actions are correct when giving a blood transfusion? Select all that apply.
options: Start the transfusion within 30 minutes of leaving the blood bank
Use Y-type tubing with normal saline
Verify with two nurses using two client identifiers
Infuse the unit over 6 hours routinely
Stay with the client for the first 15 minutes
explain: Correct: C, B, A, E — dual verification, saline-only Y-tubing, timely start, and close early monitoring catch reactions. D is wrong — each unit must finish within 4 hours to limit bacterial growth.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with tuberculosis starts isoniazid, rifampin, pyrazinamide, and ethambutol. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will stop the drugs when my cough goes away, during the current shift
I only need the drugs for two weeks, at the patient's bedside
I will take the medications for the full course and report vision changes
I can share these pills with my spouse who coughs, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: C — the full 6-9 month course prevents resistance, and ethambutol can damage the optic nerve. A and B breed drug-resistant TB. D is unsafe and illegal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which finding indicates a therapeutic effect of furosemide?
explain: Correct: D — diuresis removes excess fluid: weight drops and edema clears. A, B, and C indicate the drug is not working or fluid is accumulating.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Order: amoxicillin 45 mg/kg/day divided every 12 hours for a child weighing 18 kg. Available: 250 mg/5 mL. How many mL per dose?
explain: Correct: D — 45 x 18 = 810 mg/day; divided q12h = 405 mg/dose; 250 mg/5 mL = 50 mg/mL; 405/50 = 8.1 mL. A is one-quarter of the daily dose, C and B miscalculate the division.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which sodium level indicates hyponatremia?
explain: Correct: A — normal sodium is 135-145, so 128 is low. B and D are normal. C is hypernatremia.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client has magnesium 4.5 mg/dL with decreased reflexes and drowsiness. Which medication should the nurse anticipate?
explain: Correct: C — calcium antagonizes magnesium at the neuromuscular junction (normal Mg 1.5-2.5). D would worsen toxicity. A and B do not counteract magnesium.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are signs of hypoglycemia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, D, B — adrenergic and neuroglycopenic signs: tremor, diaphoresis, and confusion. C and E are signs of hyperglycemia/DKA.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is scheduled for a colonoscopy. Which preparation instruction is correct?
options: Continue iron supplements as usual, for now
Follow a clear-liquid diet and complete the bowel prep as directed
Eat a high-fiber meal the night before, before administering any further medication
No preparation is needed, based on the findings documented so far
explain: Correct: B — a clean colon requires clear liquids plus the prescribed bowel prep. C leaves residue. D makes the exam useless. A is wrong — iron is usually held.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which lab patterns indicate metabolic alkalosis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, A, B — metabolic alkalosis shows high pH, high bicarbonate, and often low potassium. C indicates respiratory alkalosis. D occurs in metabolic acidosis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a new cast reports increasing pain unrelieved by medication, with pale, cool fingers. What should the nurse suspect?
explain: Correct: A — pain out of proportion, pallor, and coolness signal compartment syndrome, a surgical emergency. C dismisses red flags. B would show warmth and redness. D ignores objective signs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: On post-op day 1, a client develops sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, and pleuritic chest pain. What should the nurse suspect and do first?
options: Anxiety; provide reassurance, at this stage
Pulmonary embolism; keep on bed rest, give oxygen, notify the provider
Atelectasis; encourage coughing and deep breathing, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C — sudden dyspnea with pleuritic pain after surgery is classic pulmonary embolism; immobilize, oxygenate, and escalate. D is wrong — exertion is dangerous in PE. B dismisses a lethal event. A is possible but PE fits the post-op picture best.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which value reflects a normal platelet count?
explain: Correct: B — normal platelets are 150,000-400,000. A and D are thrombocytopenic. C is thrombocytosis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are early signs of hypovolemic shock? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, F, E — early compensation brings tachycardia, anxiety, and oliguria while blood pressure is still maintained. C is a late sign. D is wrong — skin is cool and clammy. A is wrong — the heart rate rises, not falls.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a chest tube has continuous bubbling in the water-seal chamber. What does this indicate and what should the nurse do?
options: Excess suction; increase the suction setting, as documented in the plan of care
Normal finding; no action needed, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Blocked tubing; clamp the tube, on this occasion, for now
An air leak; check connections and notify the provider
explain: Correct: D — continuous water-seal bubbling means air is leaking into the system; check for loose connections and escalate. B is wrong — only tidaling is normal. C is wrong — never clamp without an order. A worsens the problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a thoracentesis, which finding requires immediate action?
options: Small amount of blood-tinged fluid, as documented in the plan of care
Mild discomfort at the site, at the patient's bedside
Dyspnea with absent breath sounds on the affected side
explain: Correct: D — dyspnea with absent breath sounds signals pneumothorax, a procedural emergency. A and B are expected. C is a normal blood pressure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with angina uses nitroglycerin. Which teaching is correct?
options: Sit or lie down, place one tablet under the tongue, and call 911 if pain persists
Take it while driving to the hospital, for now
Take five tablets at once for severe pain, before administering any further medication
Store the tablets in the bathroom medicine cabinet, in full
explain: Correct: A — sit to prevent fainting from vasodilation, one sublingual dose, and emergency help if pain continues. B is unsafe. C risks severe hypotension. D exposes tablets to heat and moisture.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are modifiable risk factors for coronary artery disease? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, F, D, C — smoking, hypertension, high LDL, and inactivity can all be changed. A and E cannot be modified.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with atrial fibrillation on warfarin is being monitored. Which finding needs immediate reporting?
options: Sudden slurred speech and facial droop
Blood pressure 132/78 mmHg, during the current shift
Small bruise at a venipuncture site, in full
explain: Correct: B — focal neuro changes signal stroke, the complication anticoagulation aims to prevent. C is a normal pressure. A is expected in afib. D is a minor, expected bruise.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which laboratory test monitors heparin infusion therapy?
explain: Correct: C — aPTT (therapeutic 1.5-2.5 times control) monitors heparin. A monitors warfarin. B and D do not guide heparin dosing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with a dissecting abdominal aortic aneurysm reports sudden tearing back pain. Blood pressure is 190/110 mmHg. What is the priority?
options: Give pain medication and reassess in one hour, before administering any further medication
Schedule a routine CT for next week, before the patient is transferred to another unit
Keep the client flat, lower blood pressure per protocol, and notify the surgeon immediately
Encourage ambulation to improve circulation, for now
explain: Correct: C — dissection needs immediate blood pressure control, bed rest, and emergency surgical evaluation. D risks rupture. A delays definitive care. B ignores the emergency.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with chronic lung disease develops systemic congestion. Which findings point to right-sided heart failure? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, C, A, E — right-sided failure causes systemic congestion: JVD, fluid weight gain, dependent edema, and liver enlargement. B and F are left-sided pulmonary signs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with pneumonia has fever, productive cough, and SpO2 90% on room air. Which finding requires immediate action?
explain: Correct: B — hypoxia below 92% needs prompt oxygen therapy. C, D, and A are expected pneumonia findings managed routinely.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which lung sound is typically heard with pneumonia?
explain: Correct: D — fluid-filled alveoli produce crackles. A suggests bronchospasm. B indicates upper airway obstruction. C suggests pneumothorax or effusion.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with myasthenia gravis undergoes edrophonium (Tensilon) testing. Which result confirms the diagnosis?
options: Improved muscle strength after the injection
No change in strength, in this case
Worsened muscle weakness, before the end of the shift
Immediate respiratory arrest, at this stage
explain: Correct: A — brief strength improvement with edrophonium confirms myasthenia gravis. C suggests cholinergic crisis instead. B is nondiagnostic. D is not an expected test outcome.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings are expected in hyperthyroidism? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, F, B — hyperthyroidism accelerates metabolism: weight loss, heat intolerance, eye changes in Graves disease, and anxiety. A and C are hypothyroid signs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Guillain-Barré syndrome has ascending weakness now reaching the arms. Which assessment is the priority?
options: Skin integrity, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Appetite, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: D — ascending paralysis can reach respiratory muscles; monitor vital capacity and negative inspiratory force for impending failure. C, A, and B matter but are not immediately life-threatening.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which is a classic sign of Parkinson's disease?
explain: Correct: A — the resting pill-rolling tremor plus rigidity and bradykinesia define Parkinson's. D occurs in cerebellar disorders. C and B are upper motor neuron or other patterns.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with ulcerative colitis asks about diet during a flare. What should the nurse teach?
options: Drink milk freely, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
There are no dietary restrictions, then reassess the patient after the intervention
Follow a low-residue, high-protein diet and avoid raw fruits and vegetables
Eat a high-fiber diet, then document the patient's response to the intervention
explain: Correct: C — low residue rests the inflamed colon while protein supports healing. D worsens diarrhea. A is wrong — lactose is often poorly tolerated. B ignores the flare.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are signs of intestinal obstruction? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, F, A, E — obstruction causes distention, obstipation, early hyperactive high-pitched sounds, and vomiting. C is the opposite pattern. D alone is not diagnostic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which meal choice indicates a client with chronic kidney disease understands the diet?
options: Grilled chicken with white rice and green beans
Baked potato with a banana, for now
Orange juice and a bran muffin, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B — controlled protein with low-potassium sides fits the renal diet. C and D are potassium-loaded. A is high in sodium and phosphorus.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings indicate thyroid storm? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, C, F, A — thyroid storm is life-threatening hypermetabolism: high fever, tachycardia, delirium, and cardiac collapse. B and E are the opposite findings.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with sickle cell anemia is in vaso-occlusive crisis. Which order should the nurse question?
explain: Correct: D — meperidine's metabolite normeperidine lowers the seizure threshold and accumulates, so it is avoided in sickle cell crisis; morphine is preferred. B, A, and C are all appropriate crisis measures.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which hemoglobin value indicates anemia in an adult woman?
explain: Correct: B — normal female hemoglobin is 12-16 g/dL, so 9 is anemic. C, D, and A are normal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which client should the nurse see first?
options: Client with a stage 1 pressure injury
Client with a migraine requesting a dark room
Client stung by a bee with stridor and hives
Client 2 days post-op ambulating in the hall
explain: Correct: C — stridor after a sting signals anaphylaxis with airway compromise. D is progressing normally. B needs comfort measures, not first. A needs prevention, not urgent care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse suspects a colleague is diverting opioids. What is the best action?
options: Document objective observations and report to the supervisor per policy
Search the colleague's locker, at this stage
Ignore it without proof, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Warn other staff to watch the colleague, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A — diversion is reported through the chain of command with factual documentation; it protects clients and the colleague's right to due process. B is illegal overreach. C ignores a safety duty. D is gossip.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which procedures require informed consent? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, B — invasive procedures and blood products need written informed consent. A and C are covered by implied consent on admission.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A competent client wants to leave against medical advice. What should the nurse do?
options: Explain the risks, notify the provider, and document the discussion and refusal
Let the client leave without any discussion, for the duration of the patient's stay
Restrain the client until the provider arrives
Have security block the exit, while keeping the patient warm and comfortable
explain: Correct: A — a competent adult may refuse care; the nurse ensures informed refusal, notifies the provider, and documents. C and D are false imprisonment. B skips the nurse's duty to inform.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which statement by the UAP requires immediate correction by the RN?
options: I assisted with the bed bath
I changed the client's sterile dressing
I helped the client to the bathroom
explain: Correct: B — sterile dressing changes require a licensed nurse; the UAP acted out of scope. D, C, and A are appropriate UAP tasks.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse asked to work a third consecutive 12-hour shift feels too fatigued to give safe care. What is the best action?
options: Work the shift anyway, at this stage
Ask the UAP to do the assessments, in accordance with facility policy
Tell the supervisor about the fatigue and the safety concern
explain: Correct: D — the nurse has a duty to protect clients and may refuse an unsafe assignment after communicating the concern. B risks harm. A abandons the team without handoff. C delegates assessment illegally.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which rights do clients have? Select all that apply.
options: Demand any treatment regardless of medical appropriateness
explain: Correct: E, C, B, A — refusal, understandable information, participation, and privacy are core client rights. D is wrong — providers are not obligated to give inappropriate or futile treatment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse discovers a medication error that reached the client but caused no harm. What is the correct sequence of actions?
options: Tell the client nothing happened, during the current shift
Document the incident report in the client's chart, on this occasion, for now
Assess the client, notify the provider, then complete the incident report
Complete the incident report first, then assess the client, in full
explain: Correct: C — client safety first: assess, notify the provider, then file the incident report (which never goes in the chart). D delays client assessment. B wrongly charts the report. A violates honesty and disclosure duties.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which task is appropriate to delegate to the LPN?
options: Reinforce wound-care teaching for a stable client
Develop the discharge plan, before the end of the shift
IV push morphine, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A — LPNs reinforce teaching for stable clients. C and B are RN-only. D is generally RN scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions demonstrate nursing accountability? Select all that apply.
options: Blaming the pharmacy for a missed dose
explain: Correct: B, E, C, D — owning errors, staying competent, supervising delegated work, and honoring scope show accountability. A shifts blame instead of owning the outcome.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Four clients arrive after a building collapse. Using START triage, which client is tagged red (immediate)?
options: Breathing 36 times per minute with a radial pulse
Breathing 20 per minute, confused, radial pulse present
Not breathing even after the airway is opened
explain: Correct: B — respirations over 30 with perfusion is red/immediate. D is expectant (black). A is minor (green). C is delayed (yellow).
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which principle is most important when the nurse delegates a task?
options: Avoid delegation entirely, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Delegate only to staff you know well, in accordance with facility policy
Delegate everything possible, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Match the task to the person's scope and competence with proper supervision
explain: Correct: D — safe delegation matches task, person, and supervision. C risks out-of-scope assignments. B is favoritism. A wastes team resources.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client with limited English needs to sign surgical consent. What should the nurse do?
options: Have the adult child interpret, before the end of the shift
Skip the interpreter to save time
Have the client sign and explain later, for now
explain: Correct: C — informed consent requires a professional interpreter; family members, especially children, must not interpret. A risks misinterpretation and coercion. D and B void true consent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are rights of delegation? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, C, E, B — the five rights are task, circumstance, person, direction/communication, and supervision/evaluation. A and F are not rights of delegation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse manager notices more medication errors on night shift. What is the best initial action?
options: Ignore the trend, before the end of the shift, for now
Punish the night nurses, in full
Collect data on when and where errors occur
Ban night-shift admissions, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C — improvement starts with data, not blame. B creates fear and hiding. D is impractical. A is negligent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which assignment is appropriate for a float nurse from the labor unit?
options: Client with a chest tube and air leak
Client with a titrating nitroprusside infusion
explain: Correct: B — floats take stable, low-complexity clients. C, D, and A need unit-specific expertise and high-acuity skills.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which findings must be reported to the provider immediately? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, A, E — critical hyperkalemia, new cardiac ischemia, and abrupt oliguria all threaten life. B is a normal pressure. D is a normal temperature.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: In SBAR communication, what does the 'R' stand for?
explain: Correct: D — Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation. The others are not part of SBAR.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A provider orders a treatment the nurse believes is unsafe, and the provider dismisses the concern. What should the nurse do?
options: Escalate through the chain of command and document the concern
Change the order independently, on this occasion
Carry out the order anyway, before the end of the shift
Quietly refuse without telling anyone, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: A — the nurse must not carry out an unsafe order; escalate and document. C violates the duty to protect. D leaves the client at risk. B exceeds nursing scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which behaviors promote effective teamwork? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, B, E — clear communication, mutual help, and role respect build safe teams. C and A destroy trust and safety.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A toddler ingests lead paint chips. Which finding is expected in lead poisoning?
options: Pinpoint pupils, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Hyperactivity and learning difficulties with abdominal pain
Excessive urination, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C — lead poisoning causes developmental delays, behavioral changes, abdominal pain, and anemia. A suggests opioids. B suggests hyperthyroidism. D is unrelated.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which items are needed for seizure precautions? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, A, C — padded rails, suction, and oxygen prepare for a seizure. D is dangerous — nothing goes in the mouth. E risks injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client on contact precautions for VRE needs transport to radiology. What should the nurse do?
options: Remove precautions during transport, at the patient's bedside
Cancel the test, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Transport without informing anyone, in practice
Cover wounds, apply a clean gown, and notify radiology of the precautions
explain: Correct: D — maintain precautions in transit: contained wounds, clean barriers, and handoff communication. B denies needed care. A and C spread infection.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which describes correct fire extinguisher technique?
options: Aim at the top of the flames, for now
Pull the pin, aim at the base, squeeze, and sweep
Use water on an electrical fire
Open all doors first, at the patient's bedside, in full
explain: Correct: B — PASS (Pull, Aim, Squeeze, Sweep) aimed at the base. A wastes agent above the fuel. C on electrical fires risks electrocution. D feeds the fire.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A nurse is preparing isolation rooms on a medical unit. Which clients should be placed on droplet precautions? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, B, A — influenza, mumps, and pertussis spread by large droplets. C and E are airborne and need N95 respirators.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with norovirus has vomiting and diarrhea. Which precautions are needed?
explain: Correct: A — norovirus spreads by contact with contaminated surfaces and stool; use gown, gloves, and strict hand hygiene. D and B target the wrong routes. C risks outbreak.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions prevent wrong-site surgery? Select all that apply.
options: The surgeon marks the operative site
explain: Correct: E, C, D, A — the Universal Protocol requires verification, site marking by the proceduralist, a team time-out, and consent review. B defeats the entire safeguard.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are standard precautions? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, A, C — hand hygiene, barrier protection for body fluids, and safe sharps handling apply to every client. D is only for droplet risks. B is prohibited.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A nurse finds a client unresponsive with an empty bottle of unknown pills nearby. What is the first action?
options: Give milk to dilute the pills, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Assess responsiveness and airway, and call the emergency response
Wait to see what happens, and report the findings to the healthcare provider
Induce vomiting, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B — airway and circulation come first, with immediate emergency help and poison control. D risks aspiration. A is ineffective. C wastes critical time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which intervention best prevents falls in a confused older adult?
options: Leave the client alone, before the end of the shift
Restrain the client in a chair, in accordance with facility policy
Hourly rounding with toileting, low bed, and call light in reach
Sedate the client, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C — proactive rounding, toileting, low bed, and access to help prevent falls without restraints. B increases injury risk. D raises fall risk. A is neglect.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which foods pose the highest choking risk for toddlers? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, D, B, C — round, firm, or sticky foods can block a toddler's airway. E is a safe texture.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with an iodine allergy needs a CT with contrast. What should the nurse do?
options: Inform the provider and radiology team before the procedure
Cancel the scan without notifying the provider, as documented in the plan of care
Proceed without telling anyone, for now
Give the contrast faster to finish quickly, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A — contrast allergy history must reach the provider and radiology for premedication or alternative imaging. C risks anaphylaxis. D worsens reactions. B bypasses the care team.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: At what age can most infants sit without support?
explain: Correct: D — independent sitting emerges around 6 months. B and C are too early. A is late.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A pregnant client with a pre-pregnancy BMI of 32 asks about recommended weight gain. What should the nurse teach?
explain: Correct: A — for obesity (BMI 30+), the recommended gain is 11-20 pounds. C is for normal BMI. D is for underweight BMI. B is unsafe.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are danger signs in pregnancy that require immediate reporting? Select all that apply.
options: Sudden gush of fluid from the vagina
Mild ankle swelling at the end of the day
explain: Correct: D, A, B, C — severe headache, vision changes, preterm contractions, and ruptured membranes can signal preeclampsia or labor. E is common and expected late in the day.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A new mother cries frequently and feels overwhelmed 5 days after delivery. What should the nurse do?
options: Tell her to stop breastfeeding, before administering any further medication
Assess severity, provide support, arrange follow-up, and screen for depression
Tell her it is normal and do nothing, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Recommend immediate hospitalization, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B — early blues are common but need assessment to catch postpartum depression; support plus follow-up is the standard. C dismisses her distress. D is premature. A is unrelated.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which cancer screenings are routinely recommended? Select all that apply.
options: Prostate cancer screening discussion for men 50 and older
explain: Correct: A, E, C, D — breast, colorectal, cervical, and prostate screening follow age-based guidelines. B is not a routine screening test.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which statement about breast self-awareness is correct?
options: Strict monthly exams on a set schedule are required, before the end of the shift
It is only needed after age 60, based on the findings documented so far
Know how your breasts normally look and feel, and report changes promptly
It replaces mammograms, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C — current guidance emphasizes knowing one's normal and reporting changes. A reflects outdated rigid teaching. B and D are false.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An 80-year-old with osteoporosis wants to start exercising. What should the nurse recommend?
options: Avoid all exercise, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Run every day, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Lift heavy weights, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Get provider clearance, then begin walking and balance exercises
explain: Correct: D — clearance plus weight-bearing walking and balance work protects bones and prevents falls. B risks fracture. A causes deconditioning. C is unsafe without supervision.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A parent asks when their child should receive the HPV vaccine. What should the nurse teach?
options: At 18 years of age, for now
explain: Correct: A — routine HPV vaccination is recommended at 11-12 years (can start at 9), before exposure. B, D, and C miss the recommended window.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client is crying quietly in bed. What is the nurse's best initial response?
options: Leave immediately to give privacy, before the end of the shift
Sit with the client and offer quiet presence
What's wrong with you?, at this stage
Don't cry, everything will be fine, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B — therapeutic presence honors the client's feelings without rushing them. D is false reassurance. A abandons the client. C is judgmental.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are therapeutic communication techniques? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, A, B — open-ended questions, listening, and reflection help clients explore feelings. C imposes the nurse's values. E blocks communication.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with borderline personality disorder idealizes one nurse and devalues another. This is an example of:
explain: Correct: C — splitting divides people into all-good or all-bad. A attributes one's feelings to others. B rejects reality. D channels impulses constructively.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with a fear of flying must travel for work. Which therapy is most appropriate?
explain: Correct: D — gradual exposure paired with relaxation treats phobias effectively. C overwhelms without preparation. B is slow for a specific phobia. A leaves the client impaired.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions are appropriate for a client with bulimia nervosa? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, C, B, D — purging causes hypokalemia and dental erosion needing surveillance, post-meal supervision interrupts purging, and consistent weights track progress. F and A reinforce the disorder.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which neurotransmitter is most targeted by SSRIs in treating depression?
explain: Correct: D — selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors raise synaptic serotonin. The others are targets of different drug classes.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client taking phenelzine (an MAOI) asks about diet. What must the nurse teach?
options: Avoid tyramine-rich foods like aged cheese, wine, and cured meats
Increase caffeine intake, as part of the patient's ongoing care
There are no food restrictions, during the current shift
Eat aged cheese freely, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A — tyramine with MAOIs can trigger hypertensive crisis. D is dangerous. C and B ignore a life-threatening interaction.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client on haloperidol develops muscle rigidity, high fever, and unstable vital signs. What should the nurse suspect?
explain: Correct: B — rigidity, hyperthermia, and autonomic instability define neuroleptic malignant syndrome, an emergency. D is milder and afebrile. C comes from serotonergic drugs. A is late-onset involuntary movement.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which measures help prevent aspiration during tube feedings? Select all that apply.
options: Give the feeding as fast as possible
Keep the head of the bed at 30 to 45 degrees
Keep the head elevated 30 to 60 minutes after feeding
explain: Correct: B, C, D, E — upright positioning, residual checks, placement verification, and post-feeding elevation all reduce aspiration. A increases aspiration and intolerance.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client must learn three-point gait with crutches for a non-weight-bearing leg. Which instruction is correct?
options: Move each leg alternately with the opposite crutch, for the duration of the patient's stay
Use the crutches only on stairs, before administering any further medication
Advance both crutches and the affected leg together, then the unaffected leg
Drag both legs forward together, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C — three-point gait: crutches and the affected leg move as one unit, then the strong leg bears the weight. A describes two-point gait. D and B are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: An older adult has liquid stool leaking around a fecal mass with abdominal cramping. What does this indicate?
explain: Correct: A — seepage of liquid stool around an impaction with cramping is classic. B is wrong — this is not normal. C would show frequent loose stools. D is a chronic pattern, not this acute picture.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which foods are high in fiber? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, C, D — whole grains, produce, and legumes provide fiber. B is refined and low in fiber. A has essentially no fiber.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with stress incontinence asks about treatment. What should the nurse teach first?
options: Restrict all fluids, on this occasion
Wear pads and accept it, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Schedule surgery immediately, at this stage, for now
Practice pelvic floor (Kegel) exercises and bladder training
explain: Correct: D — first-line treatment is pelvic muscle strengthening, timed voiding, and weight management. C is premature. A risks dehydration. B gives up on treatable symptoms.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which action promotes venous return in a client on bed rest?
options: Sit with legs dependent all day, as documented in the plan of care
Perform ankle pumps and use sequential compression devices
Cross the legs at the knees, before the end of the shift
Massage the calves vigorously, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: B — ankle pumps and compression devices move venous blood. C impedes flow. A pools blood. D can dislodge a clot.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A post-op client's wound edges separate with visible underlying tissue. What should the nurse do first?
options: Leave it open to air, and encourage the patient to report any new symptoms
Apply ointment and tape it closed, before administering any further medication
Cover with a sterile saline-moistened dressing and notify the surgeon
Push the tissue back inside, while monitoring for signs of infection at the site
explain: Correct: C — dehiscence/evisceration needs a sterile moist cover, NPO status, and immediate surgical notification. D risks contamination and injury. B is inadequate. A dries and contaminates tissue.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which are activities of daily living (ADLs)? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, E, D — basic ADLs are bathing, dressing, eating, toileting, and transferring. B is an instrumental ADL.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: lidocaine infusion 2 mg/min. Available: lidocaine 2 g in 500 mL. What is the rate in mL/hr?
explain: Correct: B — 2 g/500 mL = 4 mg/mL; 2 mg/min / 4 mg/mL = 0.5 mL/min x 60 = 30 mL/hr. The other options misconvert grams, milligrams, or minutes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medications increase bleeding risk when taken with warfarin? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — aspirin and NSAIDs impair platelets, and metronidazole inhibits warfarin metabolism. E is the preferred analgesic. C opposes warfarin, reducing its effect.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes metformin and is scheduled for a CT with contrast. Which instruction is essential?
options: Take metformin with the contrast, with the patient's safety as the stated priority
Double the metformin dose, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Stop metformin permanently, on this occasion
Tell the provider; metformin is typically held around contrast studies
explain: Correct: D — contrast can injure kidneys, and metformin with renal impairment risks lactic acidosis; it is held per protocol with renal checks. B and A are dangerous. C is unnecessary.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are signs of serotonin syndrome? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, C, D, A — hyperthermia, agitation with clonus, sweating, and rigidity reflect serotonergic excess, usually with tachycardia. E is the opposite finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication reverses the effects of warfarin?
explain: Correct: A — vitamin K restores clotting factor production. D reverses heparin. B reverses opioids. C reverses benzodiazepines.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client is prescribed IV potassium at 10 mEq/hr peripherally. Which action is essential?
options: No monitoring is needed, on this occasion, for now
Give it IV push for faster correction, in full
Infuse no faster than 10 mEq/hr with cardiac monitoring
Mix it with any available fluid, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C — potassium is never pushed; peripheral rates stay at or below 10 mEq/hr with ECG monitoring for dysrhythmias. B can cause cardiac arrest. D ignores compatibility. A skips essential monitoring.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drugs can cause ototoxicity? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, C, E — aminoglycosides, loop diuretics (especially combined), and high-dose vancomycin can damage hearing. D and A are not ototoxic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client taking a statin reports new muscle pain. What should the nurse do?
options: Tell the client to ignore it
explain: Correct: B — muscle pain may signal rhabdomyolysis; the provider should evaluate creatine kinase. A risks kidney injury. C and D are unsafe independent actions.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes spironolactone. Which lab value is most concerning?
explain: Correct: A — spironolactone is potassium-sparing, so hyperkalemia is the danger. D, B, and C are normal values.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which statements about magnesium sulfate infusion are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Therapeutic levels are 4 to 7 mEq/L for eclampsia
explain: Correct: B, D, A, E — toxicity shows as lost reflexes and respiratory depression, calcium reverses it, and levels guide therapy. C is unsafe during infusion.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication route avoids first-pass liver metabolism?
explain: Correct: C — sublingual absorption enters systemic veins directly, bypassing the liver. A, B, and D are all absorbed through the gut into the portal circulation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes levodopa/carbidopa for Parkinson's disease. Which instruction is correct?
options: Take it with a high-protein meal, during the current shift
Take it only at bedtime, for now
Stop it when feeling better, in full
Take it on an empty stomach and do not stop abruptly
explain: Correct: D — protein competes with absorption, and abrupt withdrawal can cause crisis. A blocks absorption. C and B mistime or discontinue therapy unsafely.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are side effects of calcium channel blockers? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, B, A, C — vasodilation causes headache and edema, some agents enlarge gums, and reduced gut motility causes constipation. E and F are the opposite of these drugs' effects.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with atrial fibrillation takes apixaban. Which teaching is correct?
options: Stop it before dental work without asking
Eat a consistent amount of vitamin K
Get your INR checked weekly, for now
Take it exactly as prescribed and report any bleeding
explain: Correct: D — apixaban needs no routine INR monitoring; adherence and bleeding vigilance matter. C, A, and B are warfarin rules misapplied.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which BUN and creatinine values suggest prerenal acute kidney injury?
explain: Correct: B — a BUN-to-creatinine ratio above 20:1 suggests prerenal causes like dehydration. A and D are normal. C shows intrinsic renal failure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest increased intracranial pressure in an infant? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, D, A, E — bulging fontanel, shrill cry, poor feeding, and downward eye deviation signal rising ICP in infants. B alone is not a warning sign.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which hemoglobin A1c value indicates good diabetic control?
explain: Correct: A — target A1c is generally below 7%; 5.8% reflects excellent control. C, D, and B show poor control.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client has persistent vomiting. Which arterial blood gas pattern is expected?
explain: Correct: C — losing stomach acid causes metabolic alkalosis: high pH, high bicarbonate. B is metabolic acidosis. A is respiratory alkalosis. D is normal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which actions help prevent post-op deep vein thrombosis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, E, C, D — movement, compression, exercises, and hydration keep venous blood flowing. A impedes venous return.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is on airborne precautions for tuberculosis. Which nursing action is correct?
options: Discontinue precautions after 2 days of medication, for now
No mask is needed during transport, as documented in the plan of care
A surgical mask is enough for the nurse, at the patient's bedside
Wear a fit-tested N95 respirator and keep the room door closed
explain: Correct: D — airborne precautions require a fit-tested N95 and a closed negative-pressure room. C uses the wrong mask. A is wrong — precautions continue until sputum is negative. B is wrong — the client wears a surgical mask during transport.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which vital sign changes occur with orthostatic hypotension? Select all that apply.
options: Diastolic drop of 10 mmHg or more
Systolic drop of 20 mmHg or more
Heart rate increase of 20 beats/min or more
No change in any vital sign
explain: Correct: D, A, E — orthostatic hypotension is defined by a systolic fall of at least 20, diastolic fall of at least 10, often with compensatory tachycardia. C, B, and F contradict the definition.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: After a liver biopsy, which position and monitoring are correct?
options: Sitting upright, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Right side-lying with frequent vital signs to watch for bleeding
Left side-lying with routine vitals, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Prone position, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B — right side-lying compresses the biopsy site against the mattress, and frequent vitals catch hemorrhage. C compresses the wrong side. A and D do not tamponade the site.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a new arteriovenous fistula for dialysis asks about care. Which teaching is correct?
options: Check for a thrill and bruit daily; no blood pressure or venipuncture on that arm
Sleep on the arm with the fistula, before the end of the shift
Lift weights with that arm to strengthen it, before administering any further medication
Wear a tight watch on that wrist, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A — a palpable thrill and audible bruit confirm patency; compression, BP cuffs, and needles threaten the fistula. B, C, and D all risk thrombosis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which finding after a paracentesis requires immediate action?
options: Small spot of drainage on the dressing
Mild discomfort at the site, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C — rapid fluid removal can cause hypovolemic shock. B and A are expected. D is normal and desired.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are complications of prolonged immobility? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, F, D, A — immobility causes lung collapse, clots, skin breakdown, and slowed bowels. E and B are the opposite of what immobility does.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with diabetes has a hemoglobin A1c of 10.2%. What does this indicate?
options: Excellent glucose control, on this occasion
Current hypoglycemia, at this stage, for now
Poor glycemic control over the past 2 to 3 months
Dehydration, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C — A1c reflects average glucose over 2-3 months; 10.2% is well above the under-7% target. A is the opposite. B cannot be judged from A1c. D is unrelated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with pericarditis reports sharp chest pain. Which finding is expected?
options: Pain worse when leaning forward, during the current shift
Friction rub at the left sternal border with pain eased by sitting forward
Pain radiating only to the jaw, at the patient's bedside
Massively elevated troponin, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: B — pericardial friction rub plus relief when leaning forward is classic pericarditis. A is backwards. C describes angina/MI. D fits MI, not pericarditis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are classic signs of inflammation? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, A, B, E — rubor, calor, tumor, and dolor are the cardinal signs. C alone is not an inflammatory sign.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with infective endocarditis suddenly develops slurred speech. What does this indicate and what should the nurse do?
options: Possible embolic stroke; notify the provider immediately
Expected fatigue; let the client rest
Medication side effect; hold all drugs
Anxiety; provide reassurance, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — vegetations can embolize to the brain; sudden neuro changes are an emergency. B, C, and D delay stroke evaluation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with peripheral artery disease reports leg pain when walking that eases with rest. What is this called?
explain: Correct: D — reproducible exertional pain relieved by rest is intermittent claudication. C occurs even at rest in severe disease. A is tingling. B is episodic finger vasospasm.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with a peptic ulcer vomits coffee-ground emesis. What should the nurse do first?
options: Encourage oral fluids, in accordance with facility policy
Give an antacid and reassess later, for now
Assess vital signs and notify the provider
Give ibuprofen for the pain, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C — coffee-ground emesis signals GI bleeding; assess for shock and escalate. B delays care. A worsens bleeding risk. D (NSAID) caused the problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings suggest appendicitis? Select all that apply.
options: Pain migrating to the right lower quadrant
Pain worsened by movement or coughing
explain: Correct: A, C, D, B — migratory RLQ pain, rebound tenderness, fever, and movement-exacerbated pain are classic. E is not the hallmark presentation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which vitamins are fat-soluble? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, B, A — vitamins A, D, E, and K are fat-soluble (stored in fat and liver). E and D are water-soluble B-complex and C vitamins.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with acute pancreatitis has severe epigastric pain radiating to the back. Which lab test best confirms the diagnosis?
explain: Correct: A — lipase is the most specific marker for pancreatitis. C and D reflect liver/biliary issues. B reflects muscle injury.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with cirrhosis vomits bright red blood. What is the priority?
options: Place the client in Trendelenburg, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Give fluids by mouth, before the end of the shift, for now
Encourage coughing to clear the airway, for the duration of the patient's stay
Keep NPO, monitor vital signs, and notify the provider immediately
explain: Correct: D — variceal bleeding is life-threatening; NPO, shock assessment, and emergency intervention (octreotide, endoscopy) come first. B risks aspiration. C is irrelevant. A is outdated and unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which diet is appropriate for a client with cholecystitis?
explain: Correct: B — fat triggers gallbladder contraction and pain, so low-fat eating rests it. C provokes attacks. A and D ignore the trigger.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings indicate anaphylaxis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, B, D, C — airway edema, vasodilation with hypotension, hives, and compensatory tachycardia define anaphylaxis. A is the opposite finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with anaphylaxis receives epinephrine. What should the nurse monitor most closely?
options: Nothing; one dose always resolves it
explain: Correct: D — watch for airway improvement, blood pressure response, and epinephrine effects (tachycardia); biphasic reactions can recur. A, B, and C miss the life-threatening issues.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which electrolyte imbalance most threatens a client in renal failure with muscle weakness and peaked T waves?
explain: Correct: B — failing kidneys retain potassium; hyperkalemia causes weakness and lethal dysrhythmias. C, D, and A do not produce peaked T waves.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings are typical in multiple sclerosis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, E, A — optic neuritis, paresthesias, and profound fatigue reflect demyelination. C is rheumatoid arthritis. D is not an MS feature.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with tumor lysis syndrome is at risk for which lethal complication?
options: Hypoglycemia, in accordance with facility policy
Isolated hypertension, at this stage, in practice
explain: Correct: A — massive cell breakdown floods the blood with potassium (plus uric acid and phosphate), risking fatal dysrhythmia. B, D, and C are not the hallmark dangers.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with hypercalcemia of malignancy has calcium 13.5 mg/dL. Which intervention is the priority?
options: Give isotonic IV fluids as ordered
explain: Correct: C — aggressive hydration promotes renal calcium excretion first; bisphosphonates or calcitonin follow. A worsens it. B is contraindicated. D alone does nothing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which actions are correct for a client with a new spinal cord injury? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, E, C, D — immobilize the spine, watch for bradycardia/hypotension/warm skin of neurogenic shock, logroll, and assess for spinal shock (areflexia). A and B risk further cord damage.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which finding is expected in neurogenic shock?
explain: Correct: D — loss of sympathetic tone causes vasodilation: warm dry skin, hypotension, and bradycardia. C describes hypovolemic/cardiogenic shock. B and A do not fit.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which client should the nurse assess first?
options: Client with suspected sepsis: temperature 103°F, heart rate 120, new confusion
Client awaiting discharge instructions, at the patient's bedside
Client with a chronic leg wound, and check the patient's allergy band before proceeding
Client 3 days post-op with controlled pain, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A — fever, tachycardia, and new confusion suggest sepsis needing rapid intervention. D is stable. B is routine. C is chronic and nonurgent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Two clients need the last available ICU bed: one with septic shock and one with multi-organ failure and a very poor prognosis. Hospital policy is silent. What principle should guide the decision?
options: First-come, first-served in all cases, before the end of the shift
Give the bed to the younger client, then check the patient's skin integrity at each position change
Allocate based on clinical need and likelihood of benefit, decided with the team per an ethical framework
Let the bedside nurse decide alone, then teach the patient how to perform the procedure at home
explain: Correct: C — justice requires fair allocation by need and likelihood of benefit through a team process, not age or arrival alone. B is age discrimination. A ignores clinical urgency. D places an unfair burden on one nurse.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which situations reflect the nurse's duty to report? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, C, F — abuse, impairment, reportable diseases, and harmful errors all carry reporting duties. E and D are not mandated reports.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client threatens to hit the nurse if an injection is given, then resists as the nurse gives it anyway. Which torts occurred?
explain: Correct: B — the threat is assault and the unwanted touching is battery. D is false written statements. C is unlawful confinement. A misses the intentional nature.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which task can the RN delegate to the UAP?
options: Fingerstick blood glucose on a stable diabetic client
Interpreting telemetry strips, before the end of the shift
Initial wound assessment, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A — routine fingersticks on stable clients are delegable. B, D, and C all require licensed nursing judgment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The RN observes the UAP using poor body mechanics when lifting a client. What should the RN do?
options: Do all the lifting for the UAP, before the end of the shift
Ignore it, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Intervene, demonstrate correct technique, and follow up
Report the UAP to the manager without discussion
explain: Correct: C — supervision means correcting, reteaching, and verifying in the moment. B neglects safety. D skips the teaching step. A is unsustainable and avoids the issue.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are benefits of bedside handoff report? Select all that apply.
options: It eliminates the need for documentation
It should be avoided because it takes longer
explain: Correct: A, B, F, C — bedside report engages the client, allows direct visualization, reduces errors, and improves satisfaction. E is wrong — safety gains outweigh time. D is wrong — documentation is still required.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A family insists on a treatment the medical team considers futile. What is the nurse's best action?
options: Refuse to care for the client, as documented in the plan of care
Provide the futile treatment as demanded, at the patient's bedside
Decide the outcome alone, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Request an ethics consult and support family-team communication
explain: Correct: D — ethics consultation plus facilitated communication respects all parties and seeks consensus. B provides nonbeneficial care. A abandons the client. C exceeds the nurse's role.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which document communicates end-of-life treatment preferences across care settings?
options: Work schedule, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Insurance card, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: B — POLST translates goals into portable medical orders. D, A, and C are unrelated to care preferences.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions show respect for client autonomy? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, D, A — choices, information, and honored refusals uphold self-determination. E and B undermine it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse must allocate the last dose of a scarce antidote between two clients, and no policy exists. What should the nurse do?
options: Give it to the first client seen
Escalate to leadership and the ethics committee immediately
Hide the dose to avoid deciding, during the current shift, for now
Decide based on personal values, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: B — scarce-resource decisions belong to a team process with ethical oversight, never one clinician alone. A is arbitrary. C is dereliction. D substitutes personal bias for fairness.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client asks the nurse to pray with them. What is the best response?
options: Accommodate respectfully or offer chaplain support
Preach the nurse's own beliefs, at the patient's bedside
Ignore the request, as documented in the plan of care
Refuse outright, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A — respectful accommodation or chaplain referral honors spiritual needs. D and C dismiss the client. B imposes the nurse's beliefs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse charts that a client 'is drug-seeking.' Which legal issue does this raise?
explain: Correct: D — judgmental written labels can constitute libel; chart objective facts instead. B is a threat. C is unwanted touching. A is unlawful confinement.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which tasks can the UAP perform for a client with a colostomy? Select all that apply.
options: Assist a stable client with walking
explain: Correct: E, D, B — emptying the bag, I&O, and ambulation are routine delegable tasks. C and A require licensed assessment and skill.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which client should the charge nurse assign to the new graduate RN?
options: Client with unstable diabetic ketoacidosis, at the patient's bedside
Stable client with pneumonia on oral antibiotics
Client with titrating vasoactive infusions, for now
explain: Correct: C — new graduates take stable, predictable clients. B, D, and A need experienced judgment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: What is the main purpose of trending incident reports in quality improvement?
options: To punish staff, as documented in the plan of care
To identify system patterns and prevent future harm
To increase paperwork, at the patient's bedside, for now
To satisfy curiosity, on this occasion
explain: Correct: B — trending reveals patterns for system fixes. A creates a blame culture. C and D miss the safety purpose.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which situations require a qualified medical interpreter? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, E, B, C — consent, teaching, symptom assessment, and goals-of-care talks all need accurate interpretation. D can use simple phrases or gestures.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is the best definition of fidelity in nursing ethics?
options: Doing good for others, for now
Always telling the truth, in full
explain: Correct: A — fidelity is faithfulness to promises. C is beneficence. D is veracity. B is justice.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse is subpoenaed to testify about a client's care. What should the nurse do?
options: Rewrite the chart before testifying, at the patient's bedside
Discuss the case with the media, before the end of the shift
Ignore the subpoena, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Inform risk management and testify truthfully about documented facts
explain: Correct: D — notify risk management, then give truthful testimony limited to facts and scope. C is contempt. B violates privacy. A is illegal chart tampering.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions prevent breaches of client confidentiality? Select all that apply.
options: Sharing only the minimum necessary information
explain: Correct: D, B, C, E — private discussions, secured records, minimum-necessary sharing, and identity checks protect privacy. A exposes information publicly.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A family runs a gas generator indoors during a power outage. Which findings suggest carbon monoxide poisoning?
options: Pinpoint pupils, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C — headache, dizziness, confusion, and classic cherry-red skin suggest CO poisoning; treat with 100% oxygen. D suggests opioids. A and B do not fit.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are home fire safety measures? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, B, C, F — detectors, escape plans, extinguishers, and closed doors (which slow fire spread) save lives. E and A create fire hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with an implanted pacemaker is scheduled for an MRI. What should the nurse do?
options: Verify MRI compatibility with the provider and radiology before the scan
Send the client without mentioning the device, at the patient's bedside
Cancel all future MRIs, before the end of the shift
Have the pacemaker removed first, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A — many devices are MRI-conditional but need verification and possible reprogramming; the team must confirm. B risks device malfunction. D is extreme. C is unnecessary.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which crib setup is safest for an infant?
options: Firm mattress with no soft objects
explain: Correct: D — a bare, firm sleep surface prevents suffocation. B, C, and A all add suffocation and SIDS risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which clients are at high risk for falls? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, A, D, E — sedation, blood pressure drops, poor vision, and confusion all raise fall risk. B is low risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A toddler puts a button battery in the mouth. What is the priority?
options: Give bread to push it down, for now
Wait for it to pass naturally
explain: Correct: B — button batteries cause severe esophageal burns within hours; this is an emergency. A risks more injury. D wastes critical time. C does not help.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which precautions apply when handling chemotherapy? Select all that apply.
options: Disposal in a chemotherapy waste container
explain: Correct: C, A, B, D — chemo-rated PPE, eye protection, designated waste containers, and hand hygiene protect staff. E exposes others to hazardous drugs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which measures are part of contact precautions? Select all that apply.
options: Surgical mask for every routine entry
Dedicated client equipment such as a stethoscope
explain: Correct: A, D, E, F — gown, gloves, eye protection when splashing is possible, and dedicated equipment prevent contact transmission. C is for airborne diseases. B is not required for contact alone.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: An infant with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is admitted. Which precautions are needed?
explain: Correct: C — RSV spreads by large droplets and contact with secretions. B is for airborne organisms. D is insufficient. A is for immunocompromised clients.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which action best prevents infection spread when collecting a sputum specimen?
options: Collect it in a clean drinking cup, as documented in the plan of care
Have the client cough into the open air, for now
Refrigerate the sample for a week first
Use a sterile container with hand hygiene and a mask
explain: Correct: D — sterile container, hand hygiene, and masking contain organisms. A is not sterile. C delays diagnosis. B aerosolizes pathogens.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client at risk for elopement leaves the unit unsafely. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Assess for injury when the client returns
explain: Correct: D, C, B, A — escalate, search, document, and assess on return. E is wrong — restraints are never punishment and need orders and criteria.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which home modification best prevents scald burns in older adults?
options: Set the water heater to 120°F or lower
Remove the smoke detectors, in practice
Place space heaters near the bed
explain: Correct: B — 120°F or lower prevents scalds. A increases burn risk. C removes fire warning. D is a fire hazard.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: The nurse is teaching parents of a 4-year-old about discipline. Which guidance is best?
options: Use brief time-outs and praise good behavior consistently
Spank for misbehavior, in accordance with facility policy
Ignore all misbehavior, as documented in the plan of care
Shame the child publicly, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A — consistent, brief time-outs with positive reinforcement teach effectively. B and D harm development. C ignores unsafe behavior.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are expected newborn reflexes? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, B, A, D — rooting, Moro (startle), Babinski, and stepping are present at birth. E develops months later. C is wrong — the newborn grasp is reflexive, not voluntary.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which measures help prevent osteoporosis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, B — calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing exercise, and limited alcohol protect bone. E and D weaken bone.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An Rh-negative mother delivers an Rh-positive infant. When should RhoGAM be given?
explain: Correct: C — RhoGAM within 72 hours prevents sensitization and future hemolytic disease. A mistimes it. D is too late. B risks sensitization.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A postpartum client has a boggy uterus and heavy lochia. What should the nurse do first?
explain: Correct: B — fundal massage contracts the uterus and controls bleeding; then reassess and notify. C delays the immediate intervention. D and A do not address atony.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which vaccines are recommended for adults 65 and older? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, B, E — flu yearly, pneumococcal, shingles (50+), and current COVID-19 guidance apply to older adults. F and D are not given annually.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A new mother asks about breastfeeding. Which statement indicates correct understanding?
options: I will feed every 6 hours on a strict schedule
I will give water between feedings
I will stop if my nipples hurt, for now
I will feed on demand about 8 to 12 times daily
explain: Correct: D — frequent on-demand feeding establishes supply. A is too infrequent. B is unnecessary and reduces intake. C needs lactation help, not weaning.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which newborn finding requires immediate reporting?
explain: Correct: C — central cyanosis signals hypoxia. B is normal in the first day. D and A are normal newborn findings.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client with somatic symptom disorder reports multiple pains with no organic cause. What is the best nursing action?
options: Acknowledge the distress, limit symptom focus, and teach coping skills
Ignore the complaints, before the end of the shift, for now
Tell the client it is all in their head, during the current shift
Order more diagnostic tests, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A — the distress is real to the client; validation plus coping strategies and limited reinforcement of the sick role help. C is dismissive. D reinforces somatization. B abandons the client.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are defense mechanisms? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, D — regression, suppression, and sublimation are unconscious ego defenses. E is a behavior, not a defense. B is a medical condition.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which nurse response shows empathy?
options: You should just relax, for now
Cheer up, things could be worse
I know exactly how you feel, during the current shift
It sounds like you're feeling overwhelmed
explain: Correct: D — reflection names the client's feeling without claiming it. C presumes feelings. B minimizes. A gives advice.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client is on suicide precautions. Which interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Place in a private room with a locked door
explain: Correct: B, A, E — close observation, removing means, and safe utensils protect the client. C hides the client from view. D leaves opportunity for self-harm.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are signs of delirium? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, C, E, D — delirium is acute, inattentive, fluctuating, and disorganized, often from medical causes. F and A describe dementia.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: An older adult with dementia becomes agitated at sundown. What should the nurse do?
options: Provide a calm environment with redirection and a consistent routine
Apply restraints, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Sedate routinely, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Argue with the client, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: A — sundowning responds to low stimulation, redirection, and routine. B and C increase harm. D escalates agitation.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client receiving electroconvulsive therapy asks what to expect. What should the nurse teach?
options: You will be awake during the treatment, at the patient's bedside
Temporary memory loss is common; you will be NPO beforehand
One treatment cures depression permanently, during the current shift
No consent is needed, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: B — ECT is done under anesthesia with NPO status, and short-term memory gaps are expected. A is wrong — anesthesia is used. C overpromises. D is wrong — informed consent is required.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with alcohol withdrawal has tremors and heart rate 110. Which medication should the nurse anticipate?
options: An opioid, in accordance with facility policy
