Haloperidol alone, on this occasion, for now
A benzodiazepine per the withdrawal protocol
A stimulant, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C — benzodiazepines prevent seizures and delirium tremens in alcohol withdrawal. B alone does not prevent seizures. A and D are inappropriate.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which teaching is correct for a client with a patient-controlled analgesia (PCA) pump? Select all that apply.
options: Report pain that is not relieved
Family members may push the button for the client
Only the client should push the button
explain: Correct: D, B, A, E — only the client doses, lockouts limit delivery, unrelieved pain must be reported, and breathing exercises continue. C is dangerous — proxy dosing causes overdoses.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which position is best for a client with dyspnea?
explain: Correct: A — high Fowler's lets the diaphragm descend and expands the lungs. D and B worsen breathing. C is for ARDS proning, not routine dyspnea.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with diabetes needs foot care teaching. Which statement indicates understanding?
options: I will cut my nails in a curved shape, during the current shift
I will use heating pads on my feet
I will walk barefoot to toughen my feet
I will inspect my feet daily and never go barefoot
explain: Correct: D — daily inspection and protective footwear prevent ulcers. C invites injury. A should be straight across. B risks burns with neuropathy.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which are expected signs of approaching death? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, C — irregular breathing, mottling, and oliguria signal the body shutting down. A and B are the opposite pattern.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with chronic pain uses a fentanyl patch. Which teaching is essential?
options: Share leftover patches with family, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Avoid heat sources; fold the used patch and dispose of it safely
Cut the patch in half to save money, at the patient's bedside
Apply a heating pad over the patch, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B — heat accelerates absorption and can cause overdose; used patches still contain drug and must be folded and secured. D risks overdose. C destroys the delivery system. A is illegal and dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which nutrient is most essential for wound healing?
explain: Correct: C — protein rebuilds tissue; deficiencies delay healing. A, B, and D do not drive tissue repair.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client who is NPO complains of thirst. Which action is appropriate?
options: Offer oral swabs and ice chips per orders
Give a full glass of water, at the patient's bedside
Ignore the complaint, on this occasion
Give juice, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: A — swabs and small ice chips relieve thirst without breaking NPO. B and D violate NPO. C ignores suffering.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which interventions help a client with nausea? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, A, B, D — small meals, odor avoidance, ginger, and ordered antiemetics ease nausea. C worsens reflux and nausea.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: 1000 mL normal saline over 8 hours with a 15 gtt/mL set. What is the drip rate?
explain: Correct: D — 1000/8 = 125 mL/hr; 125 x 15 / 60 = 31 gtt/min. The other options miscalculate volume, time, or drop factor.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drug is the antidote for acute iron overdose?
explain: Correct: B — deferoxamine chelates iron. A reverses opioids. D reverses benzodiazepines. C reverses heparin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are anticholinergic side effects? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, B — anticholinergics dry secretions, retain urine, and blur vision (can't see, can't pee, can't spit). E and D are cholinergic effects.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes phenytoin. Which level indicates a therapeutic range?
explain: Correct: C — therapeutic phenytoin is 10-20 mcg/mL. D is subtherapeutic. A and B are toxic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client is prescribed metronidazole. Which instruction is essential?
options: Stop when feeling better, on this occasion
Avoid alcohol during treatment and for 48 to 72 hours after
Take it with antacids, during the current shift, for now
Drink alcohol freely, at this stage, in practice
explain: Correct: B — alcohol with metronidazole causes a disulfiram-like reaction. D is dangerous. C reduces absorption. A risks treatment failure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medications require monitoring for kidney or hearing damage? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, E, D — aminoglycosides and vancomycin threaten kidneys and hearing; amphotericin E is strongly nephrotoxic. C and B lack these toxicities at normal doses.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with heart failure takes digoxin and a loop diuretic. Which diet teaching matters most?
options: No diet changes are needed, at the patient's bedside
Include potassium-rich foods in a balanced diet
explain: Correct: C — adequate potassium protects against digoxin toxicity from diuretic losses. D invites hypokalemia. A and B ignore the interaction.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which is the maximum recommended daily acetaminophen dose for most healthy adults?
explain: Correct: A — 4 g/day is the usual ceiling; less with liver disease or heavy alcohol use. B and C are single-dose amounts. D risks liver failure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are correct steps for using a metered-dose inhaler? Select all that apply.
options: Inhale slowly while pressing the canister
explain: Correct: D, E, B, A — shake, exhale, slow deep inhalation with actuation, then a breath hold for deposition. C is wrong — inhale through the mouth.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client uses timolol eye drops for glaucoma. Which assessment matters most?
explain: Correct: D — timolol is a beta blocker with systemic absorption; monitor for bradycardia and hypotension. A, B, and C miss the systemic risk.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A 20 kg child is prescribed a drug at 10 mg/kg/dose (safe range 8-12 mg/kg/dose). Available: 100 mg/5 mL. What is the correct action?
options: The dose is safe; give 5 mL
The dose is too low; double it
The dose is unsafe; hold it
The dose is safe; give 10 mL
explain: Correct: D — 10 x 20 = 200 mg, within the safe 160-240 mg range; 100 mg/5 mL = 20 mg/mL, so 200/20 = 10 mL. C and B misjudge the range. A underdoses.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drugs can prolong the QT interval? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, B, F — fluoroquinolones, macrolides, amiodarone, and IV haloperidol all prolong QT and risk torsades. A and C do not.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client in supraventricular tachycardia receives adenosine. How should the nurse administer it?
options: As a slow IV drip, for the duration of the patient's stay
By IM injection, in accordance with facility policy
As a rapid IV push with an immediate saline flush
Orally with water, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: C — adenosine's half-life is seconds; it needs a rapid push with a flush. A, B, and D would render it ineffective.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication is used to treat an acute gout attack?
explain: Correct: A — colchicine (or NSAIDs) treats acute gout flares. B prevents future attacks. D and C are unrelated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which lab findings indicate rhabdomyolysis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, F, A, B — muscle breakdown releases CK and myoglobin (dark urine) plus potassium; creatinine rises, not falls. C and E are the opposite pattern.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which is the normal range for serum magnesium?
explain: Correct: B — magnesium is 1.5-2.5 mg/dL. D is critically low. A is toxic. C is the calcium range.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with DKA has pH 7.25, HCO3 14, and potassium 5.5 mEq/L. After insulin and fluids, potassium falls to 3.0 mEq/L. What should the nurse do?
options: Stop the insulin infusion, before the end of the shift
Add potassium to the IV fluids per protocol and monitor closely
Continue fluids without potassium, on this occasion
Give IV calcium, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B — insulin drives potassium into cells; once K+ falls and urine flows, replace it per protocol to prevent lethal hypokalemia. C risks arrest. A abandons DKA treatment. D is for hyperkalemia with ECG changes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are signs of wound infection? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, E, A, C — redness, warmth, pus, and fever signal infection. B describes healthy healing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is scheduled for a cardiac stress test. Which instruction is correct?
options: Eat a heavy meal first, and notify the charge nurse of the change in condition
Exercise vigorously that morning, on this occasion
Avoid caffeine and take only approved medications per instructions
Drink coffee beforehand, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: C — caffeine and certain drugs blunt the test; follow the prep instructions. D interferes with results. A and B are unsafe or invalidating.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings indicate a positive tuberculin (Mantoux) skin test? Select all that apply.
options: 6 mm induration in a client with HIV
12 mm induration in a shelter worker
16 mm induration in a healthy adult
4 mm induration in a healthy adult with no risk factors
explain: Correct: B, A, D — cutoffs are 5 mm for HIV/close contacts, 10 mm for high-risk groups, 15 mm for low-risk adults. C is wrong — only induration is measured. E is negative.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a basilar skull fracture has clear drainage from the nose. What should the nurse do?
options: Insert a nasogastric tube, as documented in the plan of care
Pack the nose tightly, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Encourage nose blowing, during the current shift, for now
Avoid nose blowing and suctioning, keep the head elevated, and notify the provider
explain: Correct: D — clear drainage may be CSF; blowing, suctioning, or nasal tubes risk meningitis. C and B increase infection risk. A could enter the cranial vault.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are normal arterial blood gas values? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, A, B, D — these are the standard ABG ranges. E is alkalotic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with heart failure gains 2 kg in 24 hours. What should the nurse do?
options: Assess for fluid overload and notify the provider
Wait a week to recheck, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Encourage extra fluids, on this occasion
Ignore it, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — rapid weight gain signals fluid retention needing prompt evaluation and orders. D and B delay care. C worsens overload.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are risk factors for pressure injuries? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, A — immobility, moisture, and malnutrition break skin down. B and C prevent injuries.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A post-op client suddenly reports dyspnea and SpO2 drops to 88%. The nurse suspects pulmonary embolism. What is the first action?
options: Massage the legs, on this occasion, for now
Encourage ambulation, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Give oral fluids, in accordance with facility policy
Place on bed rest, give oxygen, and activate the emergency response
explain: Correct: D — immobilize, oxygenate, and escalate immediately. B and A can dislodge more clot. C does nothing for the emergency.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which white blood cell count indicates leukocytosis?
explain: Correct: A — normal WBC is 4,500-11,000; 15,000 is high. D and C are normal. B is leukopenia.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with Cushing syndrome is admitted. Which finding is expected?
options: Weight loss, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Moon face, truncal obesity, and hyperglycemia
Bradycardia, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Heat intolerance, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B — excess cortisol causes central obesity, moon face, hypertension, and high glucose. A, D, and C fit other disorders.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A post-op client becomes restless with SpO2 89%. Which additional findings indicate hypoxia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, A, E, C — tachycardia, tachypnea, cyanosis (later), and confusion reflect oxygen deprivation. D does not indicate hypoxia. B is wrong — bradycardia is a late, ominous sign, not early.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A child with epiglottitis is drooling and sitting in the tripod position. What should the nurse do?
options: Encourage fluids, before the end of the shift
Lay the child flat, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Keep the child calm and upright, avoid throat examination, and notify the provider stat
Inspect the throat with a tongue blade, under the supervision of the registered nurse
explain: Correct: C — any throat manipulation can close the airway completely; keep the child calm for emergency airway management. D can cause total obstruction. A and B are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which organism most commonly causes peptic ulcers?
explain: Correct: A — H. pylori underlies most peptic ulcers. C, D, and B are not ulcer pathogens.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with dumping syndrome after gastrectomy asks about diet. What should the nurse teach?
options: Eat small, frequent, low-sugar meals and lie down after eating
explain: Correct: B — small low-sugar meals plus reclining slow rapid gastric emptying. D triggers episodes. C washes food through faster. A does not address the mechanism.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which features distinguish Crohn's disease from ulcerative colitis? Select all that apply.
options: Can affect any part of the GI tract
Continuous inflammation starting at the rectum only
explain: Correct: E, A, C — Crohn's shows cobblestoning, full-thickness patchy inflammation anywhere in the GI tract. D and B describe ulcerative colitis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with diverticulitis has left lower quadrant pain. Which diet is appropriate during a flare?
explain: Correct: D — low residue rests the inflamed colon during a flare; fiber resumes after resolution. B worsens the flare. C and A ignore the inflammation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client has periorbital edema and cola-colored urine. Which history is most relevant?
explain: Correct: C — post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis follows strep infection by 1-2 weeks. D, A, and B are unrelated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which is the most common early sign of bladder cancer?
explain: Correct: B — painless gross hematuria is the classic first sign. D, C, and A are nonspecific or late.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are signs of increased intracranial pressure in an adult? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, E, C, D — headache, vomiting, declining consciousness, and Cushing triad changes signal rising ICP. B is wrong — the heart rate slows, not quickens.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with a spinal cord injury at T4 suddenly has blood pressure 220/120 mmHg and a pounding headache. What does this indicate?
explain: Correct: A — autonomic dysreflexia above T6 causes life-threatening hypertension from a noxious stimulus below the injury; sit the client up, remove the trigger, and notify. C, B, and D dangerously minimize it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with benign prostatic hyperplasia has urinary retention. Which medication type should be avoided?
explain: Correct: D — anticholinergics worsen retention. B, A, and C help or are appropriate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with renal calculi asks how to prevent recurrence. What should the nurse teach?
options: Restrict all fluids, on this occasion, for now
Avoid all calcium foods, at this stage, in full
Drink plenty of fluids and strain urine for stones
Stay on bed rest, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: C — high fluid intake dilutes stone-forming crystals, and straining catches stones for analysis. A concentrates urine. B is outdated advice. D promotes stasis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which precautions apply to a client with thrombocytopenia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, A, D, E — soft brushing, electric shaving, avoiding IM injections, and bleeding surveillance prevent hemorrhage. C invites injury.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which food is highest in iron?
explain: Correct: B — red meat provides heme iron, the best-absorbed form. D, C, and A are poor iron sources.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with disseminated intravascular coagulation has bleeding from IV sites and dropping platelets. Which lab pattern is expected?
options: Completely normal labs, on this occasion
Low platelets, low fibrinogen, and high D-dimer
explain: Correct: D — DIC consumes clotting factors and platelets while fibrin breaks down, raising D-dimer. C is the opposite. A and B do not fit DIC.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are symptoms of iron deficiency anemia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, C, B, A — fatigue, pallor, koilonychia, and pica (ice/clay craving) mark iron deficiency. E suggests hemolysis, not iron deficiency.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with HIV has a CD4 count of 150 cells/mm3. What does this indicate?
options: AIDS with high risk for opportunistic infections
Normal immune function, on this occasion, for now
The infection is cured, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: A — CD4 below 200 defines AIDS and brings opportunistic infection risk; antiretroviral therapy and prophylaxis are essential. B, D, and C are dangerously wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: In the obstetric triage unit, which client should the nurse evaluate first?
options: Client 2 days postpartum with normal lochia, during the current shift
Client with a ruptured ectopic pregnancy: syncope, shoulder pain, hypotension
Client with morning sickness, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C — ruptured ectopic pregnancy causes hemorrhagic shock; shoulder pain signals diaphragmatic blood irritation. D is expected. A is routine. B is normal recovery.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse's personal beliefs conflict with participating in an abortion procedure. What is the appropriate action?
options: Inform the supervisor ahead of time and arrange coverage for the client
Refuse at the last minute without telling anyone, during the current shift
Try to talk the client out of the procedure, at the patient's bedside
Abandon the assignment, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — conscientious objection requires advance notice and arranged coverage so care continues. B disrupts care. C imposes beliefs on the client. D is abandonment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are core ethical principles in nursing? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, F, C, E — autonomy, beneficence, justice, and veracity (plus nonmaleficence and fidelity) guide nursing ethics. B and D are business concerns, not ethical principles.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client has a new prescription the nurse cannot read, and the provider is unavailable. What should the nurse do?
options: Ask another nurse to interpret the handwriting, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Skip the dose silently, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Hold the medication and clarify with the pharmacist or covering provider
Guess from the context, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: C — never guess at an illegible order; clarify through the pharmacist or covering provider. D and A risk serious error. B omits needed therapy without communication.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which task can the LPN perform for a stable client?
explain: Correct: D — LPNs reinforce teaching for stable clients. B, A, and C require RN scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The RN delegates wound care to an experienced LPN but never follows up, and the wound worsens. Who is accountable?
explain: Correct: B — the delegating RN retains accountability for supervision and outcomes. C shares responsibility but the RN cannot abdicate oversight. A and D are wrong.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which information belongs in a handoff report? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, E, C, B — code status, allergies, pending results, and fall risk are safety-critical. A is social chatter, not handoff content.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A sentinel event (wrong-site surgery) occurs. What is the facility's required response?
options: Conduct a root cause analysis focused on systems
Blame the circulating nurse, on this occasion
Hide the event from the family, at the patient's bedside
Fire the surgeon immediately, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: A — sentinel events require systems-focused root cause analysis and disclosure. D and B are blame responses. C violates disclosure duties.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is the best example of veracity?
options: Keeping a promise, on this occasion
Treating everyone fairly, in accordance with facility policy
Doing good for others, at this stage, for now
Telling the truth even when it is difficult
explain: Correct: D — veracity is truth-telling. A is fidelity. C is beneficence. B is justice.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions support evidence-based practice? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, E, C, F — questioning tradition, using research, applying proven protocols, and measuring outcomes define evidence-based practice. B and A oppose it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: During a disaster with limited resources, which ethical approach should guide triage?
options: Treat the loudest clients first, for now
Treat staff family members first, at the patient's bedside
The greatest good for the greatest number
explain: Correct: C — utilitarian triage maximizes lives saved with scarce resources. A rewards volume over need. B is favoritism. D ignores survivability.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client asks to see their medical record. What should the nurse do?
options: Refuse the request, on this occasion
Charge a personal fee, for now
explain: Correct: B — clients have the right to access their records through proper channels. C denies a legal right. A and D are improper.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse gives a drug from an unclear order without clarifying, and the client is harmed. Which statement is true?
options: No one is liable, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
The nurse is also liable for failing to clarify
Only the provider is liable, during the current shift
explain: Correct: B — nurses share liability when they carry out an unclear order instead of clarifying it. C, A, and D ignore the nurse's independent duty.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are examples of nonmaleficence? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, B, A — verifying risky drugs, preventing harm, and honest reporting all avoid harm. D and E actively cause harm.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which client most needs early discharge planning?
options: Young healthy client after a minor procedure
Client with strong family support and simple medications
Older adult living alone with a new colostomy
explain: Correct: D — complex needs plus living alone demand early planning for home care, equipment, and teaching. B and C are low complexity. A needs a different approach (refusal counseling).
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: What is the nurse's role in the informed consent process?
options: Explain the procedure in full detail, for now
Sign the form for the client, as documented in the plan of care
Witness the signature and ensure the client understands
Decide for the client, in full
explain: Correct: C — the nurse witnesses, verifies understanding, and advocates; the provider explains. A is the provider's role. B and D violate autonomy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which situations require escalation through the chain of command? Select all that apply.
options: Provider unresponsive about a deteriorating client
explain: Correct: E, D, B — unanswered deterioration, unsafe staffing, and impairment all require escalation. A and C are routine matters.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which statement describes justice in health care?
options: Fair allocation of care and resources
Doing good for others, in practice
explain: Correct: A — justice is fairness in distributing care and resources. C is fidelity. B is beneficence. D is veracity.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse discovers a colleague charting care that was never given. What is the best action?
options: Confront the colleague violently, for now
Report through the chain of command
explain: Correct: C — fraudulent charting must be reported objectively through proper channels. A enables fraud. B is unprofessional. D joins the misconduct.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which strategies reduce nurse burnout and turnover? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, C, D — safe staffing, recognition, and nurse voice in decisions protect well-being. A and E drive burnout.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client overdoses on acetaminophen. Which antidote should the nurse anticipate?
explain: Correct: B — N-acetylcysteine replenishes glutathione and prevents liver failure after acetaminophen overdose. C, D, and A treat other toxicities.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are safe medication storage practices at home? Select all that apply.
options: Out of sight and reach of children
explain: Correct: D, E, C — locked, labeled, and out of children's reach prevents poisoning. B invites ingestion. A degrades medications with moisture.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with a history of falls is prescribed a new sedative. What is the priority nursing action?
options: Reassess fall risk, add precautions, and discuss alternatives with the provider
Give the sedative without any changes, in accordance with facility policy
Apply restraints, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Refuse to give the medication, then report any change to the oncoming shift nurse
explain: Correct: A — new sedatives raise fall risk; reassess, protect, and collaborate on safer options. B ignores the added risk. D exceeds nursing authority. C is not indicated.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client's clothing catches fire. What should the nurse do?
options: Run for water first, in accordance with facility policy
Use the extinguisher directly on the face
Fan the flames, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Have the client stop, drop, and roll, and smother the flames
explain: Correct: D — stop, drop, and roll plus smothering stops the burning fastest. B aims chemicals at the airway. C feeds the fire. A wastes time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions prevent injury from medical equipment? Select all that apply.
options: Checking that alarms are on and audible
explain: Correct: A, E, C, D — working alarms, intact cords, proper training, and prompt reporting prevent harm. B (alarm fatigue) endangers clients.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is about to be defibrillated. Which safety action is essential?
options: Call 'clear' and ensure no one is touching the client or bed
Keep hands on the chest, in accordance with facility policy
Stand in a puddle of water, as documented in the plan of care
Continue compressions during the shock, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — everyone must be clear of the client and bed to avoid shock injury. B, C, and D expose rescuers to the current.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which interventions are part of the ventilator-associated pneumonia prevention bundle? Select all that apply.
options: Head of bed at 30 to 45 degrees
explain: Correct: D, C, E, A — elevation, oral care, and DVT/ulcer prophylaxis form the VAP bundle. B increases aspiration risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Standard precautions apply to which body fluids? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, A, E — standard precautions cover blood, all body fluids except sweat, nonintact skin, and mucous membranes. D is excluded. C is not a fluid.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A chemotherapy spill occurs on the floor. What should the nurse do first?
options: Mop it with plain water, using the equipment available at the bedside
Wipe it up barehanded with paper towels
Don chemotherapy-rated PPE and use the spill kit per protocol
Leave it for housekeeping, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C — chemo spills need rated PPE and a spill kit to protect staff. B exposes skin. A spreads the drug. D abandons a hazard.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which disinfectant kills Clostridioides difficile spores on surfaces?
options: Alcohol-based cleaner, on this occasion, for now
Water only, going forward, in full
explain: Correct: B — only sporicidal agents like bleach kill C. difficile spores on surfaces. C, A, and D are ineffective against spores.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions are correct during a code blue? Select all that apply.
options: Bring the crash cart and defibrillator
Crowd into the room to watch
explain: Correct: E, B, A, C — compressions, equipment, role clarity, and documentation drive resuscitation. D obstructs the team.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which oxygen safety rule is most important?
options: Cover oxygen vents, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Use oil-based products on oxygen equipment, during the current shift
Post no-smoking signs and keep oxygen away from flames
explain: Correct: D — oxygen fuels fire; no smoking or open flames nearby. C, B, and A create fire or equipment hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A 14-year-old is preoccupied with identity and peer acceptance. Which developmental stage is this?
explain: Correct: B — adolescence centers on identity formation. C is school age. A is young adulthood. D is older adulthood.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are signs of toilet training readiness? Select all that apply.
options: Stays dry for 2 hours or more
Tells when they need to go
explain: Correct: B, E, F, C — bladder control, comprehension, interest, and signaling need show readiness around 18-24 months. D is too young physiologically. A is unrelated.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which teaching promotes testicular health? Select all that apply.
options: Self-exams are only needed after age 60
Roll each testicle gently between thumb and fingers
explain: Correct: D, C, F, E — monthly exams starting in adolescence, prompt reporting, warm relaxed tissue, and proper technique aid detection. B misses the at-risk young adult years. A is wrong — provider exams are still needed.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: At what age do most children say their first words?
explain: Correct: D — first meaningful words emerge around 12 months. C and A are cooing/babbling stages. B is late.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A pregnant client asks about fetal kick counts. What should the nurse teach?
options: Count 10 movements within 2 hours and report decreased movement
Count once a week, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
There is no need to monitor movement, at the patient's bedside
Kick counts are unreliable, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — 10 movements in 2 hours is the standard; decreased movement needs prompt evaluation. C, B, and D dismiss a key safety tool.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which statements about lochia are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Lochia progresses from rubra to serosa to alba
Lochia nigra is the final stage
explain: Correct: C, D, A, B — lochia changes color and progresses rubra to serosa to alba over about 6 weeks. F is wrong — foul odor suggests infection. E does not exist.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An older adult retiring feels lost without work. Which response best supports healthy adjustment?
options: Just rest and do nothing, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Avoid all new activities, on this occasion
Explore meaningful activities and social connections
Suggest withdrawing from friends, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: C — new roles, purpose, and connection ease the retirement transition. A, B, and D promote isolation and decline.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which skin change should be reported as a possible melanoma?
options: Long-standing age spot, on this occasion, for now
Mole with irregular borders and color change
Smooth skin tag, at this stage
Small symmetric freckle, unchanged, in this case
explain: Correct: B — asymmetry, border irregularity, and color change (ABCDE) warn of melanoma. D, C, and A are benign patterns.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client with antisocial personality disorder tries to split staff against each other. What is the best nursing approach?
options: Ignore all of the behavior, for now
Punish the client, in accordance with facility policy
Set firm, consistent limits with whole-team consistency
explain: Correct: C — consistent boundaries and team communication defeat manipulation. D rewards it. B is punitive, not therapeutic. A misses needed limit-setting.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which behaviors suggest depression? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, B, D — anhedonia, sleep disturbance, and poor concentration mark depression. A suggests mania. C is the wrong direction; appetite usually decreases.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which defense mechanism channels unacceptable impulses into acceptable activities?
explain: Correct: A — sublimation redirects impulses constructively. D rejects reality. C attributes feelings to others. B retreats to earlier behavior.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions help a client with generalized anxiety disorder? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, E, A — relaxation, exercise, and challenging anxious thoughts reduce anxiety. C worsens it. D is impossible and avoidant.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are positive symptoms of schizophrenia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, A — hallucinations, delusions, and disorganized speech are added (positive) symptoms. C and B are negative symptoms (loss of function).
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with dementia asks for their deceased mother. Using validation therapy, which response is best?
options: Your mother died 20 years ago, in full
It sounds like you miss your mother
explain: Correct: D — validation honors the feeling behind the words instead of confronting with painful facts. C causes distress. A is demeaning. B is unjustified.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client in crisis is denying the situation. What is the nurse's priority?
options: Ensure safety and offer supportive presence
Make all decisions for the client, before the end of the shift
Force the client to face reality, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — crisis care starts with safety and support; confrontation comes later if at all. D overwhelms. C abandons. B strips autonomy.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which statement about Wernicke's encephalopathy is correct?
options: It is caused by vitamin B12 deficiency
explain: Correct: B — thiamine deficiency causes Wernicke's (confusion, ataxia, nystagmus); glucose without thiamine worsens it. C is dangerous. A is wrong — it is treatable. D names the wrong vitamin.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions manage chronic constipation? Select all that apply.
options: Education to avoid chronic stimulant laxative use
explain: Correct: E, A, B, D — fiber, fluids, activity, and avoiding laxative dependence restore function. C worsens constipation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which diet is prescribed first after surgery once bowel function returns?
options: Regular diet, before the end of the shift
No diet at all, in accordance with facility policy
High-fat diet, for the duration of the patient's stay
Clear liquids, then advance as tolerated
explain: Correct: D — clear liquids first, advancing stepwise as tolerated. A is too much too soon. C and B are inappropriate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with diarrhea needs perineal care. What is the priority?
options: Scrub the skin vigorously, on this occasion
Leave the skin soiled until the bath
Cleanse gently and apply a barrier protectant
explain: Correct: C — gentle cleansing plus barrier cream prevents excoriation. A damages skin. B invites breakdown. D burns irritated tissue.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which actions prevent foot drop during prolonged bed rest? Select all that apply.
options: Letting the feet hang unsupported off the mattress
explain: Correct: F, D, A, C — dorsiflexion support, sneakers, ROM, and exercises prevent contracture. E and B cause the very deformity being prevented.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with pruritus from liver disease asks for relief. What should the nurse teach?
options: Take hot baths, at the patient's bedside
Use cool compresses and moisturizers, and keep nails short
Wear wool clothing, in accordance with facility policy
Scratch vigorously, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B — cool moisture soothes while short nails limit skin damage. A worsens itching. D breaks skin. C irritates.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: How should dentures be cared for?
options: Share cleaning containers, for the duration of the patient's stay
Clean with hot water, as documented in the plan of care
Remove, brush daily, and store in water or denture solution
Wear them constantly, even while sleeping, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C — daily brushing and moist storage protect dentures and gums. D invites infection. B warps dentures. A spreads germs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: An unconscious client needs eye care. What should the nurse do?
options: Lubricate the eyes and keep the lids closed
Skip eye care, on this occasion
Rub the eyes periodically, in this case
Leave the eyes open to air, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A — artificial tears and lid closure prevent corneal drying and ulcers. D dries the cornea. C injures it. B neglects it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which nursing actions support adequate nutrition in older adults? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, A, E, C — manageable portions, assistive tools, appealing food, and company improve intake. D discourages eating.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: infuse 500 mL over 4 hours using a 60 gtt/mL microdrip set. What is the drip rate?
explain: Correct: D — 500/4 = 125 mL/hr; with microdrip, mL/hr equals gtt/min, so 125 gtt/min. The other options misapply the drop factor.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication reverses anticholinergic toxicity?
explain: Correct: B — physostigmine restores cholinergic activity. C reverses opioids. A reverses benzodiazepines. D reverses heparin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are important considerations for nitroprusside infusion? Select all that apply.
options: Thiocyanate levels are monitored with prolonged use
It must be protected from light
It is given as an IV bolus
explain: Correct: E, B, D, C — nitroprusside drops pressure fast, cyanide/thiocyanate accumulate with prolonged use, and light degrades it. A is wrong — reflex tachycardia is the concern. F is wrong — it is a titrated infusion.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes buspirone for anxiety. Which teaching is correct?
options: It works immediately, on this occasion, for now
Stop it abruptly when calm, at the patient's bedside
Never drive again, before the end of the shift
It takes 1 to 2 weeks for full effect and does not sedate like benzodiazepines
explain: Correct: D — buspirone needs time to work and lacks the sedation and dependence of benzodiazepines. A overpromises. B risks relapse. C is excessive.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client is prescribed allopurinol. Which finding requires immediate reporting?
explain: Correct: A — rash can herald Stevens-Johnson syndrome; stop the drug and notify. B, C, and D are minor side effects.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which statements about corticosteroid inhalers are correct? Select all that apply.
options: They are not rescue inhalers for acute attacks
explain: Correct: E, A, B, F — rinsing prevents thrush, these are daily controllers (not rescue drugs), and stopping invites relapse. C is wrong — they are long-term therapy. D describes rescue inhalers.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with overactive bladder takes oxybutynin. Which side effect should the nurse warn about?
explain: Correct: C — oxybutynin is anticholinergic: dry mouth, constipation, and urinary retention are expected. A, D, and B are the opposite effects.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which vitamin is given with isoniazid to prevent neuropathy?
explain: Correct: B — pyridoxine prevents isoniazid-induced peripheral neuropathy. D, A, and C do not.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drugs increase bleeding risk? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D — anticoagulants and antiplatelets all raise bleeding risk. E is safe at normal doses. C promotes clotting.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes zolpidem for insomnia. Which teaching is essential?
options: Take it at bedtime and rise slowly because of fall risk
Mix it with alcohol for better sleep, at the patient's bedside
Drive immediately after taking it, on this occasion
Take it in the morning, for now
explain: Correct: A — bedtime dosing with fall precautions is the safe pattern. D mistimes it. C and B are dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Ceftriaxone 1 g IM is ordered. After reconstitution the concentration is 350 mg/mL. How many mL should the nurse give?
explain: Correct: C — 1000 mg / 350 mg/mL = 2.86 mL, rounded to 2.9 mL. The other options miscalculate the concentration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which factors increase the risk of digoxin toxicity? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, D, C, E — low potassium, low magnesium, high calcium, and poor renal clearance all potentiate digoxin. B is wrong — hyperkalemia is seen in toxicity but does not increase risk the way hypokalemia does.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with myasthenia gravis takes pyridostigmine. Which finding indicates cholinergic crisis?
options: Dry mouth, on this occasion, for now
Constipation, at this stage, in practice
Improved muscle strength, in accordance with facility policy
Excessive salivation, diarrhea, and worsening weakness
explain: Correct: D — too much acetylcholine causes SLUDGE symptoms plus weakness; edrophonium worsens it (unlike myasthenic crisis). C is the therapeutic effect. A and B are anticholinergic signs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication is commonly used for motion sickness?
explain: Correct: B — meclizine is an antihistamine for motion sickness. C, A, and D are unrelated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client's thyroid labs return. Which results point to hyperthyroidism? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, C, F — hyperthyroidism shows low TSH, high T4, and often TSI antibodies in Graves disease. E and D indicate hypothyroidism. A is typically low in hyperthyroidism.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which is the normal fasting blood glucose range?
explain: Correct: D — fasting glucose is normally 70-100 mg/dL. B is hypoglycemic. A and C are hyperglycemic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is hyperventilating from anxiety. Arterial blood gases: pH 7.48, PaCO2 30 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L. Which acid-base imbalance is present?
explain: Correct: C — high pH with low PaCO2 and normal bicarbonate is respiratory alkalosis from blowing off CO2. D would show high HCO3. A and B would show low pH.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which actions are correct after a bronchoscopy? Select all that apply.
options: Report large amounts of bloody sputum
Keep NPO until the gag reflex returns
explain: Correct: E, F, A, C — protect the airway until the gag returns, watch breathing, and report significant bleeding. B risks aspiration. D is unnecessary.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client has white stools after a barium swallow. What should the nurse teach?
options: This is normal; drink extra fluids to pass the barium
Remain NPO, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Report it immediately as abnormal, for now
explain: Correct: A — barium lightens stools for a day or two; fluids help clear it. C alarms unnecessarily. D alone is not the teaching. B is wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which labs help diagnose myocardial infarction? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, E, D — troponin (most specific), CK-MB, and early myoglobin mark cardiac injury. B reflects heart failure stretch. C reflects clot breakdown.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a new pacemaker is being discharged. Which teaching is essential?
options: Check your pulse as taught, report dizziness, and avoid strong magnets
Avoid all exercise forever, before the end of the shift
Never use a microwave again, during the current shift
No follow-up is needed, under the supervision of the registered nurse
explain: Correct: A — pulse checks, reporting symptoms, and avoiding strong electromagnetic interference protect pacemaker function. B is excessive. C is a myth — microwaves are safe. D skips essential device checks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are normal adult vital sign ranges? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, E, D — these are standard adult ranges. B is hypertensive. A is hypoxemic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with diabetes shows the Somogyi effect. Which pattern is seen?
options: Gradual rise without any nighttime low
Consistently normal readings, on this occasion
Nighttime low blood sugar followed by morning high
Morning hypoglycemia, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: C — nocturnal hypoglycemia triggers rebound morning hyperglycemia. D is the opposite. B shows no effect. A describes the dawn phenomenon.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are complications of blood transfusion? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, A, C, E — fever/chills, hemolysis, volume overload, and allergy are classic transfusion reactions. B is not a transfusion complication.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client refusing blood transfusion for religious reasons is bleeding, and the provider asks the nurse to transfuse anyway. What should the nurse do?
options: Transfuse when the family leaves the room, in accordance with facility policy
Refuse to violate the client's rights and escalate through the chain of command
Transfuse as ordered, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Sedate the client first, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B — a competent adult's refusal stands; the nurse advocates and escalates rather than overriding autonomy. C, A, and D violate the client's rights.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which urine specific gravity indicates concentrated urine?
explain: Correct: D — normal is 1.005-1.030; 1.030 is maximally concentrated. B, A, and C are dilute.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with complete heart block has heart rate 38 and is dizzy. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: A beta blocker, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C — symptomatic bradycardia needs atropine first, then transcutaneous or permanent pacing. D worsens block. B and A are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with heart failure asks how to prevent fluid buildup at home. Which self-care measures should the nurse teach? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, E, C, B — less sodium, daily weights, fluid limits, and tolerated activity control failure. F risks decompensation. D overloads sodium.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Raynaud's phenomenon asks about triggers. What should the nurse teach?
options: No precautions are needed, for now
Immerse hands in ice water, before the end of the shift
Cold exposure is harmless, in practice
Keep hands warm; avoid cold, stress, and smoking
explain: Correct: D — cold, stress, and nicotine trigger vasospasm; warmth and smoking cessation prevent attacks. C, B, and A invite episodes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which blood pressure change is expected in a normal pregnancy?
options: No changes at all, in practice
explain: Correct: B — blood pressure normally dips slightly in the second trimester. C signals preeclampsia. A and D are incorrect.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with cardiac tamponade shows jugular vein distention, hypotension, and muffled heart sounds. What is the priority?
options: Notify the provider stat and prepare for pericardiocentesis
Watch and wait, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Give fluids by mouth, during the current shift
Encourage ambulation, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A — Beck's triad means the heart cannot fill; emergency pericardiocentesis is needed. C, D, and B delay life-saving care.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings indicate ulcerative colitis? Select all that apply.
options: Continuous inflammation starting at the rectum
explain: Correct: C, A, B — ulcerative colitis causes bloody diarrhea with continuous rectal-upward mucosal inflammation and urgency. D and E are Crohn's features.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with GERD asks about lifestyle changes. What should the nurse teach?
options: Elevate the head of the bed and avoid late-night meals
Eat large, spicy meals, in accordance with facility policy
Lie flat right after eating, at the patient's bedside
Wear tight belts, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A — elevation and smaller, earlier meals reduce reflux. C, B, and D worsen it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with a perforated peptic ulcer has a rigid, board-like abdomen. What is the priority?
options: Give the client food, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Discharge home, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Give antacids only, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Keep NPO, notify the surgeon immediately, and prepare for surgery
explain: Correct: D — perforation is a surgical emergency; NPO, fluids, antibiotics, and prompt surgery come first. A, C, and B are dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which hepatitis type most commonly spreads by the fecal-oral route?
explain: Correct: B — hepatitis A (and E) spread fecal-orally. A, C, and D spread by blood and body fluids.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are signs of peritonitis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, A, C, D — rigidity, rebound pain, fever, and tachycardia signal peritoneal inflammation. B is the opposite finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with abruptio placentae has a rigid uterus and dark red vaginal bleeding. What is the priority?
options: Encourage ambulation, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Send the client home, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Monitor maternal vitals and fetal heart tones continuously and prepare for emergency delivery
Perform frequent vaginal exams, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C — abruption threatens mother and fetus; continuous monitoring and readiness for emergency delivery are critical. D is unnecessary and risky. B and A are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with placenta previa has painless bright red vaginal bleeding. Which action is contraindicated?
explain: Correct: C — vaginal exams can provoke catastrophic bleeding when the placenta covers the os. D, A, and B are all appropriate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Fetal monitoring shows late decelerations. What should the nurse do first?
options: Encourage pushing, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Reposition the client, give oxygen, stop oxytocin, and notify the provider
Continue monitoring only, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Increase the oxytocin, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: B — late decelerations signal uteroplacental insufficiency; intrauterine resuscitation comes first. C delays action. A and D worsen fetal hypoxia.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: During the initial newborn assessment, which findings are considered normal? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, B, A — acrocyanosis, caput, and Babinski are normal newborn findings. D signals hypoxia. C signals dehydration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: What is the normal fetal heart rate range?
explain: Correct: A — the normal baseline is 110-160 beats/min. B is bradycardic. C and D are tachycardic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with hyperosmolar hyperglycemic state has glucose 900 mg/dL, no ketosis, and altered consciousness. What is the priority?
options: Give IV insulin push only, then report the outcome to the registered nurse
No treatment is needed, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Encourage oral fluids only, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Begin aggressive IV fluid resuscitation with electrolyte monitoring
explain: Correct: D — profound dehydration drives HHS; isotonic fluids first, then insulin, with close electrolyte watch. A alone is unsafe. C is inadequate. B is wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are risk factors for type 2 diabetes? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, D, A, B — obesity, genetics, older age, and hypertension raise risk. E protects against diabetes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: An infant of a diabetic mother is at highest risk for which complication?
explain: Correct: B — maternal hyperglycemia drives fetal insulin production; after birth, the insulin persists and drops the newborn's glucose. A, C, and D are not the hallmark risks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: At the start of the shift, the nurse reviews four postpartum clients. Who needs assessment first?
options: Postpartum client 1 day after delivery with normal lochia, before the end of the shift
Postpartum client with a boggy fundus soaking a pad in 15 minutes
explain: Correct: C — boggy uterus with heavy bleeding signals postpartum hemorrhage. A is normal recovery. D and B are routine.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client has a seizure from eclampsia. What is the priority action?
options: Restrain the client, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Insert an oral airway during the seizure, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Leave to get medication, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Protect from injury, maintain the airway, call for help, and prepare magnesium sulfate
explain: Correct: D — protect, oxygenate, get help, and treat the cause with magnesium sulfate; never restrain or force the airway. A and B cause injury. C abandons the client.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are signs of postpartum hemorrhage? Select all that apply.
options: Soaking a perineal pad in 15 minutes
explain: Correct: E, D, A, F — uterine atony with heavy bleeding plus shock signs define hemorrhage. C and B are normal findings.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Umbilical cord prolapse is noted during labor. What is the priority action?
options: Position knee-chest, use a gloved hand to lift the presenting part off the cord, and call for help
Push the cord back inside, because the priority is completing the assigned tasks on schedule, on this occasion
Wait and watch, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Encourage pushing, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — relieve cord compression with position and manual elevation while mobilizing emergency delivery. B contaminates and compresses. D worsens compression. C wastes time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The RN is assigning tasks to the UAP for the shift. Which assignment is within the UAP's scope?
explain: Correct: D — routine specimen collection is delegable. C, B, and A require licensed judgment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A new graduate is struggling with time management. As preceptor, what is the best action?
options: Take over all of the client's care, before the end of the shift
Help prioritize, model organization, and give constructive feedback
Ignore the struggle, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Belittle the graduate, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: B — coaching with prioritization and feedback builds competence. A prevents learning. D destroys confidence. C abandons the preceptee.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are the nurse's roles in disaster response? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, B, D, E — nurses triage, staff shelters, give psychological first aid, and watch for outbreaks. C and A exceed nursing scope.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse experiences moral distress over a care decision. What is the best action?
options: Voice concerns through proper channels and seek ethics support
Ignore the feelings, for the duration of the patient's stay
Quit immediately, in accordance with facility policy
Refuse all future assignments, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — moral distress is addressed through team discussion and ethics resources, not avoidance. C is premature. B buries the issue. D is abandonment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which statement is an example of slander?
options: A personal opinion, as part of the patient's ongoing care
A true statement, at this stage
A spoken false statement harming someone's reputation
A written false statement, on this occasion
explain: Correct: C — slander is spoken defamation. D is libel. B and A are not defamation.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse manager is evaluating staff for annual reviews. Which behaviors show accountability in practice? Select all that apply.
options: Checking on tasks given to the UAP
Owning up to a missed dose
explain: Correct: F, D, B, E — owning mistakes, staying competent, supervising delegated work, and truthful charting show accountability. C and A violate it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The unit is short-staffed and the nurse is given an assignment that feels unsafe. What is the best action?
options: Refuse without any documentation, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Voice the concern, document the objection, and accept the assignment while protecting client safety
Ignore the concern, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Abandon the unit, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: B — communicate, document (safe harbor where available), and do not abandon clients. D is abandonment. A skips the professional record. C ignores safety.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is an example of a breach of confidentiality?
options: Discussing a client in the elevator
Discussing a client in a private room
explain: Correct: C — public discussions expose protected information. D, B, and A protect it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client with limited health literacy needs discharge teaching. What should the nurse do?
options: Use complex medical terms, on this occasion, for now
Skip the teaching, before the end of the shift, in full
Hand over a thick booklet only, in accordance with facility policy
Use teach-back with plain language and written reinforcement
explain: Correct: D — teach-back with simple words and handouts confirms understanding. C overwhelms. B omits needed teaching. A confuses.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are steps of the nursing process? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, F, C, A — assessment, diagnosis, planning, implementation, and evaluation (implementation is the applied step). B and D are not nursing process steps.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which client should be assigned to the most experienced RN?
options: Client with sepsis on titrating norepinephrine
Routine post-op client, at this stage
Stable pre-op client, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: A — unstable clients on vasoactive drips need the most skilled nurse. D, C, and B suit less experienced staff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: What is the primary purpose of a root cause analysis?
options: To delay care improvements, at this stage
To identify system factors and prevent recurrence
To punish those involved, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B — root cause analysis fixes systems, not people. C creates blame. D and A miss the point.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which indicate effective delegation? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, A, C, E — clear direction, right person, feedback, and supervision make delegation safe. F is dumping. B guarantees failure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which ethical term means doing good for others?
explain: Correct: D — beneficence is doing good. C is self-determination. B is fairness. A is truth-telling.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Visitors claiming to be relatives demand another client's information, but the nurse is unsure of their identity. What should the nurse do?
options: Verify their relationship and the client's consent before sharing anything
Share only the diagnosis, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Call security immediately, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Share everything they ask for, then report the outcome to the registered nurse
explain: Correct: A — verify identity and authorization; disclose nothing without the client's permission. D and B violate privacy. C is premature.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are quality indicators in health care? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, E, C, B — falls, pressure injuries, infections, and satisfaction measure care quality. A and F do not.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A child drinks kerosene. What should the nurse advise?
options: Induce vomiting immediately, during the current shift, for now
Give milk to neutralize it, using the equipment available at the bedside
Do not induce vomiting; seek emergency care and call poison control
Wait and watch at home, based on the findings documented so far
explain: Correct: C — hydrocarbons aspirate easily; vomiting increases lung injury, so get emergency care instead. A risks aspiration pneumonitis. B does not help. D wastes time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are safe practices for handling soiled linen? Select all that apply.
options: Hold it away from the uniform
explain: Correct: A, E, F, B — bag at the bedside, glove up, keep it off the uniform, and wash hands. D aerosolizes organisms. C contaminates the floor and staff.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client on oxygen is found smoking in the bathroom. What is the priority?
options: Ignore it, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Discharge the client immediately, at this stage
Yell at the client, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Remove the cigarette, secure the oxygen safely, assess for injury, and reinforce safety
explain: Correct: D — eliminate the fire hazard, check for burns, and re-educate. A ignores a lethal risk. C is unprofessional. B is premature.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which technique best prevents back injury when lifting?
options: Bend the knees, keep the load close, and avoid twisting
Twist while lifting, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Bend at the waist, on this occasion, for now
Lift heavy loads alone, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — knees bent, load close, and no twisting protect the spine. C, B, and D all invite injury.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A nurse finds a frayed electrical cord on an IV pump. What should the nurse do?
options: Use it anyway, on this occasion
Hide it in the closet, during the current shift
Remove it from service, tag it, and report it
Wrap the cord with tape, at this stage, in practice
explain: Correct: C — damaged equipment is tagged out and reported. A risks electrocution. D is an unsafe repair. B endangers the next user.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is the correct way to wear a surgical mask?
options: Hang it around the neck between clients
Cover the nose and mouth; change it when damp
Reuse it for a week, for now
Below the nose, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B — masks must seal over nose and mouth and are changed when moist. D leaves the nose exposed. C and A contaminate and degrade protection.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which measures prevent health care-associated infections? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, A, B — hand hygiene, asepsis, isolation compliance, and wise antibiotic use all cut infections. C spreads them.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are examples of medical asepsis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, D, E, B — clean technique reduces organisms. A and F are surgical asepsis, a stricter standard.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with active tuberculosis needs transport to radiology. What should the nurse do?
options: Transport without notifying anyone, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Have the client wear a surgical mask, notify the department, and staff wear N95 respirators
Cancel the test, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Transport without a mask, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, for now
explain: Correct: B — the client wears a surgical mask to contain droplets while staff wear N95s, with advance notice. D, C, and A are unsafe or deny care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which container is correct for sharps disposal?
options: Linen bag, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Recycling bin, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A — sharps need rigid, labeled, leak-proof containers. D, C, and B expose others to sticks.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client is choking. Which responses are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Back slaps and chest thrusts for an infant
Encourage coughing with a partial obstruction
Abdominal thrusts for complete obstruction in an adult
explain: Correct: C, E, A — let a partial obstruction clear itself, use thrusts for complete adult obstruction, and use back slaps/chest thrusts for infants. B is prohibited unless the object is visible. D can worsen obstruction.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which firearm safety teaching is correct for a home with children?
options: No precautions are needed, during the current shift
Let children handle guns freely, as documented in the plan of care
Keep guns loaded and accessible, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Store firearms locked and unloaded, with ammunition locked separately
explain: Correct: D — locked, unloaded, with ammunition stored separately prevents tragedy. C, B, and A invite disaster.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A school-age child follows game rules and works hard for grades. Which developmental task is this?
explain: Correct: C — school-age children build industry through mastery and rules. D is infancy. B is toddlerhood. A is preschool.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are examples of preoperational thinking in a preschooler? Select all that apply.
options: Focusing on one aspect of a situation
explain: Correct: E, D, F, A — egocentrism, animism, magical thinking, and centration mark the preoperational stage. B comes with concrete operations. C comes with formal operations.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which measures help prevent skin cancer? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, F, A, E — sunscreen, cover, timing, and self-checks reduce risk. C and D increase ultraviolet damage.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: During a prenatal visit, the nurse counsels a client about iron needs. Which teaching is correct?
options: Avoid all iron supplements, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Take iron only on a full stomach, before the end of the shift
Iron needs decrease in pregnancy, for the duration of the patient's stay
Iron needs increase; take it with vitamin C and expect dark stools
explain: Correct: D — pregnancy raises iron needs; vitamin C aids absorption and dark stools are normal. C and A are wrong. B reduces absorption.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An older adult has bruises, seems fearful, and is missing medications. What must the nurse do?
options: Report to adult protective services per mandatory reporting laws
Confront the suspected abuser alone, before the end of the shift
Wait for definite proof, on this occasion
Ignore it, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A — suspected elder abuse must be reported; nurses are mandatory reporters. D and C fail the duty. B is unsafe.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are expected changes of aging? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, B, D, C — skin, reflexes, vision, and bone all decline with age. F and E are the opposite of aging.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A teenager with diabetes ignores the treatment plan and feels invincible. Which approach is best?
options: Punish the teen, as documented in the plan of care
Involve the teen in goal-setting using motivational interviewing
Take over all diabetes management, during the current shift
Lecture and threaten, on this occasion
explain: Correct: B — adolescent autonomy plus collaborative goals improves adherence. D, C, and A provoke resistance.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which exercise is best for an older adult with arthritis?
explain: Correct: C — low-impact activity protects joints while building strength. B and A damage joints. D causes deconditioning.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client hears command hallucinations telling them to hurt others. What is the priority?
options: Tell the client to obey the voices, and make sure the patient understands the instructions given
Ignore the report, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Assess safety, ensure a safe environment, and do not leave the client alone if at risk
Argue that the voices are not real, then document the patient's response to the intervention
explain: Correct: C — command hallucinations demand immediate safety assessment and protection. A is dangerous. B neglects risk. D argues instead of securing safety.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are therapeutic responses to a silent, withdrawn client? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, B, D — quiet presence, gentle observation, and offering another time respect the client's pace. A is coercive. E abandons. F blocks the client's space.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which defense mechanism involves making up for a weakness in one area by excelling in another?
explain: Correct: D — compensation offsets perceived weakness with strength elsewhere. C rejects reality. A attributes feelings to others. B retreats to earlier behavior.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions are appropriate for opioid withdrawal? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, B, E, A — supportive care plus clonidine for symptoms; opioid withdrawal is miserable but rarely life-threatening. C precipitates severe withdrawal and is contraindicated.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with chronic schizophrenia shows little motivation, flat affect, and social withdrawal. Which of these are negative symptoms? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, A, C, F — flat affect, lack of motivation, anhedonia, and poverty of speech are losses of function. B and E are positive symptoms.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with illness anxiety disorder constantly seeks medical tests. What is the best nursing action?
options: Acknowledge the anxiety, limit repeated reassurance, and teach coping skills
Tell the client they are imagining it, at the patient's bedside
Ignore the client, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Order more tests, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: A — validation plus coping strategies breaks the reassurance cycle. D reinforces the disorder. B is demeaning. C abandons.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with major depression starts sertraline. Which teaching is essential?
options: It has no side effects, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time
It takes weeks to work; keep taking it and report worsening mood or suicidal thoughts
Stop it once you feel happy, in accordance with facility policy
It works immediately, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, in this case
explain: Correct: B — SSRIs need 2-4 weeks; stopping early or missing the suicidality warning (especially early treatment) is dangerous. D overpromises. C risks relapse. A is false.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which is the priority nursing diagnosis for a client in acute mania?
explain: Correct: B — hyperactivity, poor judgment, and no sleep make injury the top risk. C, A, and D are lower priorities.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which measures prevent aspiration in a client with dysphagia? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, F, C, E — upright posture, small bites, proper textures, and double swallows protect the airway. B and D invite aspiration.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which comfort measure helps a client with hemorrhoids?
explain: Correct: D — warm sitz baths soothe and reduce swelling. C and A worsen congestion. B aggravates hemorrhoids.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort
