q: A client with venous stasis ulcers needs teaching. Which statement indicates understanding?
options: I will elevate my legs and wear compression stockings
I will avoid all walking, at the patient's bedside
I will stand in one place all day
I will cross my legs often, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A — elevation and compression counteract venous pooling. C and D worsen it. B causes deconditioning.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which are appropriate comfort measures for dyspnea? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, C, D, A — upright posture, cool airflow, breathing technique, and calm surroundings ease breathlessness. B worsens it. F increases anxiety.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with arterial ulcers on the toes needs foot teaching. Which is most important?
options: Apply tight compression wraps, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Soak the feet in hot water, during the current shift
Protect the feet from trauma, avoid pressure, and keep them warm
Walk barefoot, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C — arterial ulcers need protection and warmth without compression that further cuts blood flow. A worsens ischemia. B burns insensate feet. D invites injury.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which food must a client with celiac disease avoid?
explain: Correct: C — celiac disease requires a gluten-free diet; wheat contains gluten. D, A, and B are gluten-free.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with an ileostomy asks about expected output. What should the nurse teach?
options: No output is expected, on this occasion
Bloody output is normal, at this stage
Formed stools twice a day, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B — ileostomy output is liquid and continuous since the colon is bypassed. D describes a colostomy. A and C are wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which are normal findings with a urostomy? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, F, C, D — intestinal mucus, continuous flow, healthy pink stoma, and adequate output are normal. A suggests infection. E signals a poor appliance seal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Order: heparin bolus 80 units/kg for a client weighing 70 kg. How many units should the nurse give?
explain: Correct: A — 80 x 70 = 5,600 units. The other options miscalculate the weight-based dose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication treats symptomatic bradycardia?
explain: Correct: D — atropine speeds the heart. C, B, and A all slow it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are side effects of hydralazine? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, F, E, B — vasodilation causes headache, flushing, and reflex tachycardia; long use can trigger lupus-like symptoms. D and C are the opposite effects.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes clonidine for hypertension. Which teaching is essential?
options: Double the dose if one is missed, during the current shift
Do not stop abruptly; rebound hypertension can occur
No monitoring is needed, on this occasion, for now
Stop it anytime you feel well, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B — abrupt clonidine withdrawal causes dangerous rebound hypertension. D and A are unsafe. C skips needed blood pressure checks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client is prescribed trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole. Which instruction is essential?
options: Drink plenty of fluids and report any rash
Take it with antacids only, for now
Stop after two days, during the current shift
Restrict fluids, on this occasion, in full
explain: Correct: A — fluids prevent crystalluria and rash can signal serious reactions. D risks kidney injury. B and C are wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with increased intracranial pressure is prescribed mannitol. Which nursing considerations apply? Select all that apply.
options: Monitor for signs of pulmonary edema
Give as a rapid IV push
explain: Correct: A, C, F, E — mannitol crystallizes (filter needed), shifts fluid rapidly (watch lungs), and needs I&O, electrolytes, and neuro checks. D is wrong — it is infused carefully. B ignores real risks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes bupropion for depression. Which teaching is essential?
options: Crush the extended-release tablet, for the duration of the patient's stay
It is safe with active bulimia, at the patient's bedside
Report seizures; avoid alcohol; do not use it with eating disorders
Take it only at bedtime, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: C — bupropion lowers the seizure threshold, especially with eating disorders or alcohol withdrawal. B is contraindicated. D mistimes dosing. A destroys the formulation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drug class is ondansetron?
explain: Correct: D — ondansetron is a 5-HT3 antiemetic for nausea and vomiting. C, A, and B are unrelated classes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medications can raise blood glucose? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, B, E — steroids, thiazides, and atypical antipsychotics all raise glucose. A and D lower it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes ketorolac. Which teaching is essential?
options: Take it on an empty stomach, in accordance with facility policy
It has no serious risks, at the patient's bedside
Short-term use only, up to 5 days, because of stomach and kidney risks
Use it for months at a time, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C — ketorolac is limited to 5 days due to GI bleeding and renal injury. D is dangerous. A worsens GI risk. B is false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A 15 kg child is prescribed 50 mg/kg/day divided three times daily. Available: 250 mg/5 mL. How many mL per dose?
explain: Correct: D — 50 x 15 = 750 mg/day; divided TID = 250 mg/dose; 250 mg/5 mL = 50 mg/mL, so 5 mL. The other options misdivide the daily dose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are cautions with long-term proton pump inhibitor use? Select all that apply.
options: Take before the first meal of the day
explain: Correct: F, D, E, B — long-term PPI use raises fracture, B12, and C. difficile risks; dosing before breakfast is standard. C is wrong — they take days to work fully. A is wrong — interactions exist.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia needs anticoagulation. Which drug is appropriate?
explain: Correct: B — fondaparinux does not cross-react with HIT antibodies. C is contraindicated. A alone is unsafe in acute HIT. D is inadequate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which laxative type is safest for long-term use?
explain: Correct: A — bulk-forming fiber is safe long-term. C causes dependence. B risks aspiration and vitamin loss. D disrupts normal function.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which labs suggest inflammation or infection? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, E, F, A — CRP, ESR, high WBC, and procalcitonin all mark inflammation or bacterial infection. D and B are nonspecific alone.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which is the normal serum osmolality range?
explain: Correct: C — normal osmolality is 275-295 mOsm/kg. D is dilute. B and A are severely concentrated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with COPD exacerbation has arterial blood gases: pH 7.32, PaCO2 48 mmHg, HCO3 24 mEq/L. Which interpretation is correct?
explain: Correct: A — low pH with high PaCO2 is respiratory acidosis from CO2 retention. D would show low HCO3. C and B would show high pH.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which actions are correct after a bone marrow biopsy? Select all that apply.
options: Remove the pressure dressing at once
Assess pain and give analgesics as ordered
explain: Correct: E, A, B, D — pressure, positioning on the site, bleeding checks, and pain control are standard. F risks bleeding. C removes needed pressure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with atrial fibrillation has an apical pulse of 96 and a radial pulse of 82. What does this indicate?
explain: Correct: B — the apical-radial gap is a pulse deficit from beats too weak to reach the wrist. A is wrong — they should match. C and D are unrelated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest a dislodged tracheostomy tube? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, E, B — distress, displacement, subcutaneous emphysema, and falling SpO2 signal a lost airway. D is the opposite finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client dislodges a new tracheostomy tube in the first week after placement. What should the nurse do?
options: Leave the stoma open, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Force the tube back in, before administering any further medication
Cover it with gauze only and notify the registered nurse of the patient's status
Call for help, ventilate with a bag-mask, and prepare for provider reinsertion
explain: Correct: D — the tract is not mature; blind reinsertion can create a false passage, so ventilate and get expert help. B risks false passage. A and C abandon the airway.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are normal urine characteristics? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, E, C, A — normal urine is straw-to-amber, clear, pH 4.5-8, with adequate output. B suggests infection. D suggests sediment or infection.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A Holter monitor is ordered for 24 hours. Which instruction is correct?
options: Remove it at night, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Keep a diary of activities and symptoms, and keep the device dry
Shower as usual, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Exercise vigorously to test it, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B — the diary links symptoms to rhythm strips, and moisture ruins the device. C damages it. A interrupts monitoring. D is unsafe and unneeded.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are early signs of compartment syndrome? Select all that apply.
options: Absent pulses as the very first sign
Pain out of proportion to the injury
explain: Correct: D, F, B, C — disproportionate pain, paresthesia, pallor, and stretch pain appear early. A is a late sign. E is the opposite finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: On post-op day 2, a client has no bowel sounds, nausea, and abdominal distention. What should the nurse suspect and do?
options: Paralytic ileus; keep NPO, notify the provider, and prepare for a nasogastric tube
Discharge the client, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Normal recovery; feed the client, before administering any further medication
Give laxatives immediately, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: A — absent sounds with distention and nausea signal ileus; rest the bowel and decompress. C feeds an obstructed gut. D is premature. B is unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which lab value best reflects long-term nutritional status?
explain: Correct: D — albumin reflects protein stores over weeks. A reflects immediate glucose. B reflects electrolytes. C reflects infection.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with aortic stenosis reports fainting with exertion. Which finding is expected?
options: No murmur at all, on this occasion, for now
Diastolic murmur only, at this stage
Bounding pulses, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C — the classic triad is angina, syncope, and dyspnea with a systolic murmur. B is wrong — the murmur is systolic. A and D do not fit.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings indicate venous insufficiency? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, B, E — edema, hemosiderin staining, medial ankle ulcers, and aching eased by elevation mark venous disease. F and D are arterial signs.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with thrombophlebitis has a red, warm, tender calf vein. What should the nurse do?
options: Apply warm compresses, elevate the leg, and avoid massaging
Apply ice only, in accordance with facility policy
Massage the leg firmly, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Encourage vigorous exercise, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — warmth and elevation soothe; massage can dislodge clot. C risks embolism. D is excessive. B alone is less effective.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which position best improves venous return from the legs?
explain: Correct: C — elevation uses gravity to return venous blood. A, B, and D all impede return.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A young athlete collapses during a game, and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy is suspected. What is the priority?
options: Drive the athlete home, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Give water and have them rest, for the duration of the patient's stay
Wait to see if they wake up
Begin CPR, apply the AED, and activate the emergency response
explain: Correct: D — sudden collapse suggests lethal dysrhythmia; immediate CPR and defibrillation save lives. B, A, and C waste the resuscitation window.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are signs of acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS)? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, F, C, A — refractory hypoxemia, bilateral infiltrates, poor compliance, and tachypnea define ARDS. B is wrong — oxygen does not fix it. D is wrong — lungs sound wet.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with flail chest has paradoxical chest movement. What does this mean?
options: Normal chest movement, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
The injured segment moves opposite to the rest of the chest during breathing
No chest movement at all, and compare the findings with the patient's baseline values
Wheezing on expiration, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: B — the free-floating segment moves inward on inspiration and outward on expiration. A, C, and D misdescribe it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A child with croup has a barky cough and stridor. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: Cool mist and corticosteroids per orders
Throat exam with a tongue blade
Hot steam treatment, on this occasion, in full
explain: Correct: A — cool mist, dexamethasone, and possibly racemic epinephrine treat croup; keep the child calm. C misses the viral cause. B agitates and worsens obstruction. D is not the therapy.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which test confirms cystic fibrosis?
explain: Correct: C — elevated sweat chloride confirms cystic fibrosis. D, B, and A do not diagnose it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are complications of cystic fibrosis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, F, E, B — thick secretions block lungs, pancreas, and intestines, causing infection and malnutrition. A is not the hallmark. D is backwards — sweat salt is high.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Huntington's disease shows choreiform movements. Which inheritance pattern applies?
explain: Correct: B — Huntington's is autosomal dominant; one affected parent gives a 50% risk. D, C, and A are incorrect patterns.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis asks about the disease course. What should the nurse teach?
options: It improves with vigorous exercise, during the current shift
It affects only memory, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, on this occasion, for now
Antibiotics will cure it, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Progressive muscle weakness usually occurs with intact thinking; care focuses on function and comfort
explain: Correct: D — ALS destroys motor neurons while cognition typically remains; care is supportive. A, B, and C are false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Bell's palsy cannot close one eye. What is the priority eye care?
options: Leave the eye open to air
explain: Correct: D — artificial tears, taping the lid closed at night, and sunglasses prevent corneal injury. C dries the cornea. A injures it. B neglects it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which can trigger trigeminal neuralgia pain? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, C, B, F — chewing, wind, touch, and tooth brushing trigger the lightning-like facial pain. D and A are not typical triggers.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which finding is expected in nephrotic syndrome?
explain: Correct: A — nephrotic syndrome means heavy proteinuria (>3.5 g/day) with edema, hyperlipidemia, and low albumin. C, B, and D are the opposite pattern.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with pyelonephritis has fever and flank pain. Which assessment finding is expected?
options: No fever at all, on this occasion, in practice
explain: Correct: B — CVA tenderness plus fever marks kidney infection. C fits cystitis. D and A contradict pyelonephritis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which measures help prevent urinary tract infections? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, A, E, F — fluids, post-coital voiding, front-to-back wiping, and avoiding spermicides reduce UTI risk. B promotes bacterial growth. C disrupts normal flora.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with systemic lupus erythematosus asks about sun exposure. What should the nurse teach?
options: No precautions are needed, at this stage
Tanning beds are safe, on this occasion
Avoid sun exposure and use sunscreen
Sunbathe to improve the rash, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C — photosensitivity means sun triggers lupus flares; protection is essential. D, A, and B invite flares.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: During morning assignments on a pediatric unit, four children need assessment. Which child must the nurse assess first?
options: Child waiting for routine discharge teaching, as documented in the plan of care
School-age child with a mild barky cough, before the end of the shift
Toddler whose fever broke overnight, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Infant with bloody mucus stools who pulls the legs up during episodic crying
explain: Correct: D — bloody mucus ('currant jelly') stools with colicky pain suggest intussusception, a surgical emergency. B is mild croup. A and C are routine.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A child with Kawasaki disease has had fever for 6 days with strawberry tongue and conjunctivitis. What is the priority intervention?
options: IV immune globulin and aspirin per protocol with cardiac monitoring
Cold compresses only, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Antibiotics only, on this occasion, for now
Discharge home, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: A — IVIG plus aspirin prevents coronary artery aneurysms, the feared complication. C alone is inadequate. D and B ignore the cardiac risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are signs of dehydration in an infant? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, C, F, B — sunken fontanel, absent tears, oliguria, and dry membranes mark infant dehydration. D and E are normal findings.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: An infant has projectile nonbilious vomiting and a palpable olive-shaped abdominal mass. What should the nurse suspect and prepare for?
options: Gastroenteritis; prepare for discharge, for now
Constipation; give an enema, during the current shift
Pyloric stenosis; stabilize fluids and electrolytes, then surgery
Intussusception; prepare for barium enema, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: C — projectile vomiting with an olive mass is pyloric stenosis; correct the hypochloremic alkalosis first, then pyloromyotomy. D has currant jelly stools instead. A and B miss the surgical problem.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which task can the UAP perform after a client dies?
options: Notify the family of the death
explain: Correct: B — postmortem care is an appropriate UAP task. C and D are provider or RN roles. A is done by the RN or provider.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The nurse delegates EKG acquisition to the UAP, but the tracing is uninterpretable. What should the nurse do?
options: Assess the technique, reteach, and verify a readable tracing
Ignore the poor tracing, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Blame the UAP, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Do all EKGs personally from now on, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — supervision means assessing, reteaching, and verifying the outcome. C is punitive. D avoids the teaching role. B accepts bad data.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are principles of palliative care? Select all that apply.
options: Addresses physical, emotional, and spiritual needs
explain: Correct: A, C, E, D — palliative care relieves suffering alongside any treatment, using a team for whole-person needs. B describes hospice timing narrowly. F is the opposite of its goal.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse is asked to participate in a legal procedure they believe is unethical. The nurse objects. Which statement is true?
options: The nurse must participate regardless, in accordance with facility policy
The nurse may abandon the client, based on the findings documented so far
The nurse should sabotage the procedure, at the patient's bedside
Conscience protections apply, but the nurse must ensure the client still receives care
explain: Correct: D — conscience clauses protect the nurse while requiring continuity of care through reassignment. A ignores the protection. B is abandonment. C is misconduct.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is an example of paternalism in health care?
options: Respecting cultural values, in accordance with facility policy
Deciding for a competent client without their consent
Honoring a client's refusal, on this occasion, for now
Providing full information, at this stage, in full
explain: Correct: B — paternalism overrides autonomy 'for the client's own good.' C, D, and A respect autonomy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions support a just culture? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, A, D, E — just culture learns from systems and shared reporting. B and C create fear and hiding.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A competent client refuses a life-saving blood transfusion, and the family begs the nurse to transfuse. What is the correct course?
options: Sedate the client and transfuse, for now
Get a court order in every case, before the end of the shift
Honor the competent refusal and support the family
Transfuse to save the client's life, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C — a competent adult's informed refusal stands, even when life-threatening; the nurse supports the grieving family. D, B, and A violate autonomy.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which element is required for valid informed consent?
options: Family signature in all cases, during the current shift
No information is needed, as part of the patient's ongoing care
A competent client given adequate information voluntarily
explain: Correct: D — competence, disclosure, and voluntariness make consent valid. A is only for incompetent clients. C and B are invalid.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse photographs a client's wound for the chart without asking permission. Which legal issue arises?
explain: Correct: C — photographing without consent invades privacy. A is a threat. B is unwanted touching. D requires harm from substandard care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are components of the I-PASS handoff? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, D, E, B — Illness severity, Patient summary, Action list, Situation awareness, and Synthesis by receiver. A and C are not handoff components.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which is the best measure of nursing care quality?
explain: Correct: B — outcomes show whether care worked. A, C, and D measure activity, not quality.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: What is benchmarking in quality improvement?
options: Cutting the budget, at the patient's bedside
Punishing low performers, on this occasion
Ignoring the data, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — benchmarking measures against the best to find improvement targets. C, B, and D misuse the concept.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which findings require immediate provider notification? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, A, C, D — chest pain, severe hypotension, hypoxia, and acute mental status change are all emergencies. E and B are routine.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which statement about whistleblower protection is true?
options: Good-faith safety reports are legally protected
Reporting is always punished, for now
No protection exists for nurses, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A — laws protect workers who report safety concerns in good faith. D, C, and B are false.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A disaster shelter houses 200 evacuees with limited staff. Which approach should guide the nurse's priorities?
options: Treat each person fully before moving to the next, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Close the shelter, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Serve staff members first, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Prioritize life-threatening needs, infection control, and basic needs for the most people
explain: Correct: D — population-focused triage does the greatest good with scarce resources. A is too slow for 200 people. C is favoritism. B abandons the mission.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are barriers to effective communication? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, C, B, F — jargon, noise, literacy gaps, and cultural blind spots block understanding. D and A improve it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client ingests organophosphate pesticide and shows SLUDGE symptoms (salivation, lacrimation, urination, defecation, GI upset, emesis). Which antidotes should the nurse anticipate?
explain: Correct: B — atropine dries secretions and pralidoxime reactivates cholinesterase. C, A, and D treat other poisonings.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are signs of salicylate toxicity? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, D, C, F — tinnitus, hyperventilation, anion-gap acidosis, and GI upset mark salicylate poisoning. A and E are the opposite findings.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has an unknown respiratory illness during an outbreak. What is the safest initial precaution approach?
options: Surgical mask only, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
No precautions, in accordance with facility policy
Airborne precautions including an N95 until the pathogen is identified
Standard precautions only, as part of the routine care for this patient
explain: Correct: C — start with the highest level (airborne) and step down once the organism is known. D, B, and A risk transmission.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is the correct way to remove contaminated gloves?
options: Snap them off quickly, on this occasion
Pull from the fingertips, at this stage, for now
Grasp the outside at the wrist and peel off inside out
Reuse them, going forward, in full
explain: Correct: C — peeling from the wrist inside out contains contamination. B, A, and D spread it.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A laboratory specimen must be transported to the lab. Which action is correct?
options: Label it later at the lab, using the equipment available at the bedside
Label at the bedside, place in a biohazard bag, and transport promptly
Leave it at the nurses' station, at the patient's bedside
Carry it in a uniform pocket, based on the findings documented so far
explain: Correct: B — bedside labeling prevents mix-ups; biohazard bags and prompt transport protect everyone. A, D, and C risk errors and exposure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which hand hygiene method is preferred when hands are visibly soiled?
explain: Correct: A — visible soil needs soap and water; alcohol rubs are for clean-looking hands. C does not clean hands. D spreads infection.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which actions help prevent surgical site infections? Select all that apply.
options: Hair removal with clippers, not razors
explain: Correct: C, E, D, A — antiseptic shower, clippers, on-time antibiotics, and normothermia prevent infection. B causes micro-cuts that harbor bacteria. F exposes the wound.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are fire prevention measures in health care facilities? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, A, C, B — no smoking, safe oxygen handling, alarms, and drills prevent and prepare for fire. D and E create deadly hazards.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client with disseminated shingles has widespread vesicles. Which precautions are needed until lesions crust?
options: Droplet precautions only, in this case
explain: Correct: D — disseminated zoster spreads by airborne and contact routes until every lesion crusts. B, C, and A are insufficient.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: An unvaccinated nurse sustains a needlestick from a hepatitis B-positive client. What is the best response?
options: Wait for symptoms, on this occasion
Give hepatitis B immune globulin and start the vaccine series
Do nothing, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Give antibiotics, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: B — HBIG plus the vaccine series prevents infection after exposure. C risks chronic hepatitis. D does not treat viruses. A wastes the prophylaxis window.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client has a seizure in the hospital. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Turn the client to the side if possible
Insert an oral airway during the seizure
explain: Correct: C, B, E — protect, time, and side-lying positioning are correct. F risks dental and airway injury. D causes musculoskeletal harm. A risks aspiration before full recovery.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is the safest position for a client having a seizure in bed?
explain: Correct: A — side-lying keeps the airway open and lets secretions drain. B risks aspiration. C and D are unsafe during a seizure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A 3-year-old insists on doing everything 'by myself' and says 'no' to almost everything. How should the nurse advise the parents?
options: Shame the child, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Give in to every demand, using the equipment available at the bedside
Offer limited choices and stay consistent; this negativism is normal
Punish the defiance, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: C — toddler negativism asserts autonomy; limited choices channel it safely. D and A damage development. B teaches no limits.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are normal preschool behaviors? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, A, B, C — imaginary friends, playing with peers, normal fears, and magical thinking are typical at 3-5 years. D comes in adolescence. F is unrealistic.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which guidance is safe for exercise during pregnancy? Select all that apply.
options: Stopping for pain, bleeding, or dizziness
explain: Correct: E, F, B, D — moderate exercise, avoiding trauma and heat, warning-sign awareness, and Kegels are all safe. C risks fetal harm. A is contraindicated.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: At what age should solid foods be introduced to an infant?
explain: Correct: D — solids start around 6 months when the infant can sit and swallow. C and A are too early. B delays needed nutrients.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A parent asks about giving honey to a 6-month-old. What should the nurse teach?
options: Honey prevents allergies, on this occasion, for now
Honey is fine at any age, at the patient's bedside
Give honey every day, at this stage, in full
Avoid honey until 1 year because of botulism risk
explain: Correct: D — infant botulism spores in honey can paralyze young infants; wait until 1 year. B, C, and A are dangerous.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which are signs of healthy infant attachment? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, A, B, D — seeking comfort, stranger/separation wariness, social smiling, and calming with contact show secure attachment. F and E suggest attachment problems.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An older adult is worried about driving safety. Which advice is best?
options: Drive faster to keep up with traffic, using the equipment available at the bedside
Stop driving immediately at age 65, during the current shift
Get regular vision and hearing checks and adapt driving habits
Ignore the concern, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C — sensory checks plus adaptations (daytime driving, familiar routes) keep older drivers safe. B is arbitrary. A and D are dangerous.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which is the best way to keep an older adult's skin healthy?
options: Hot water and harsh soap, at the patient's bedside
Gentle cleansing, moisturizers, and sun protection
Alcohol-based skin products, on this occasion
No bathing at all, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: B — gentle care plus moisture and sun protection preserve fragile skin. A, D, and C damage it.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A client rambles continuously without pause. Which response is therapeutic?
options: Gently refocus: 'Let's go back to what you were saying about...'
Leave the room, for the duration of the patient's stay
Change the subject abruptly, on this occasion
Interrupt rudely, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: A — gentle refocusing validates while guiding back to the topic. D is disrespectful. B abandons. C confuses.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are examples of immature defense mechanisms? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, A, C, D — projection, acting out, regression, and denial distort reality to manage anxiety in immature ways. Sublimation and humor are mature, adaptive defenses.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which defense mechanism involves unconsciously expressing the opposite of one's true feelings?
explain: Correct: C — reaction formation flips unacceptable feelings into their opposite. A rejects reality. B attributes feelings to others. D retreats to earlier behavior.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions are appropriate for panic disorder? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, B, F, A — breathing control, trigger awareness, CBT, and relaxation treat panic. D is maladaptive avoidance. E provokes panic.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are risk factors for postpartum depression? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, F, D, C — depression history, isolation, stress, and unplanned pregnancy raise risk. E and B protect against it.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with seasonal affective disorder asks about treatment. What should the nurse teach?
options: Bright light therapy as directed, plus regular activity
No treatment exists, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Stay in the dark all winter, during the current shift, for now
Avoid all light, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — morning bright-light therapy with exercise and sometimes medication treats seasonal depression. C, B, and D are wrong.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with schizophrenia speaks in 'word salad.' Which response is best?
options: Laugh along, as documented in the plan of care
I'm having trouble following you; can you tell me what you need?
Pretend to understand, in accordance with facility policy
Argue about the meaning of the words, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B — honestly acknowledge the difficulty and focus on needs and feelings. C is dishonest. D argues pointlessly. A is demeaning.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which is the most reliable way to assess suicide risk?
options: Asking the family only, on this occasion
Guessing from the client's mood, for now
A no-suicide contract, at this stage
Direct questions about thoughts, plan, and means
explain: Correct: D — direct assessment of ideation, plan, means, and intent is the standard. C is not reliable alone. B and A are indirect.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are nonpharmacologic comfort measures for labor? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, F, E, C — movement, breathing, water, and support ease labor pain. D and B increase pain and slow labor.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which pain scale is best for a 4-year-old child?
options: No scale is usable, for now
explain: Correct: B — FACES matches preschoolers' concrete thinking. C suits older children and adults. A is too advanced. D ignores available tools.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with sleep apnea is prescribed CPAP. Which teaching is essential?
options: Use it every night with proper mask fit, and clean it as directed
No follow-up is needed, while observing the patient for any adverse reaction
Share the mask with a partner, in accordance with facility policy
Use it only when feeling tired, and wash hands before and after the procedure
explain: Correct: A — nightly use with a good seal treats apnea; cleaning prevents infection. D is inadequate. C spreads germs. B skips needed monitoring.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which are components of good sleep hygiene? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, F, B, D — regular hours, screen limits, good sleep environment, and daytime activity promote sleep. A stimulates. E disrupts nighttime sleep.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with anorexia nervosa is admitted severely malnourished. What is the priority in starting nutrition?
options: Begin a high-calorie diet immediately, before the end of the shift
Force-feed the client, on this occasion, for now
Withhold all nutrition, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Start nutrition slowly with close electrolyte monitoring for refeeding syndrome
explain: Correct: D — rapid refeeding shifts phosphate, potassium, and magnesium dangerously; start slow and monitor. A risks fatal refeeding syndrome. C starves further. B is abusive.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which diet is lowest in residue?
explain: Correct: C — clear liquids leave almost no residue. D, B, and A all leave significant residue.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client with lactose intolerance asks about diet. What should the nurse teach?
options: Avoid dairy or use lactase-treated products, and find alternate calcium sources
No dietary changes are needed, at the patient's bedside
Drink more milk, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care
Eat only cheese, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — avoid lactose or replace the enzyme, and protect bones with other calcium sources. C worsens symptoms. B ignores the problem. D still contains lactose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which actions help prevent skin tears in older adults? Select all that apply.
options: Adhesive tape directly on fragile skin
explain: Correct: F, E, D, B — moisture, gentle handling, padding, and sleeves protect fragile skin. A scratches it. C tears it on removal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: For a 70-kg client in hypertensive emergency, sodium nitroprusside is ordered at 3 mcg/kg/min. The IV bag holds 50 mg in 250 mL and must be protected from light. Calculate the pump setting in mL/hr.
explain: Correct: B — 3 x 70 = 210 mcg/min, or 12.6 mg/hr; concentration 50 mg/250 mL = 0.2 mg/mL, so 12.6/0.2 = 63 mL/hr. The other options misconvert micrograms to milligrams or minutes to hours.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drug is given with atropine for organophosphate poisoning?
explain: Correct: D — pralidoxime reactivates cholinesterase alongside atropine. C, B, and A treat other toxicities.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which are important considerations for theophylline therapy? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: B, E, F, A — theophylline has a narrow range; toxicity brings tachycardia, GI upset, and seizures. C is the opposite effect. D is false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client carries an epinephrine auto-injector. Which teaching is correct?
options: Store it in the freezer, as part of the routine care for this patient
Inject it into a vein, before administering any further medication
Press it into the outer thigh through clothing, hold, and call 911
It can only be used once in a lifetime, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C — outer thigh through clothing, hold several seconds, then emergency care. B is wrong — it is intramuscular. D and A are false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client is prescribed sucralfate. Which instruction is correct?
options: Take it at the same time as antacids
Take it on an empty stomach
explain: Correct: D — sucralfate coats the ulcer best on an empty stomach. C and A reduce contact. B binds it up.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which statements about warfarin reversal are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Fresh frozen plasma if PCC is unavailable
4-factor prothrombin complex concentrate for life-threatening bleeding
Vitamin K for elevated INR without bleeding
explain: Correct: D, C, F, B — vitamin K for non-urgent reversal, PCC (or plasma) plus holding warfarin for emergencies. E is wrong — heparin adds bleeding. A continues the problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A woman of childbearing age is prescribed misoprostol. Which warning is essential?
options: It is safe in pregnancy, before the end of the shift
Take it with alcohol, at the patient's bedside, for now
It can cause miscarriage; avoid in pregnancy and use contraception
It has no warnings, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: C — misoprostol is abortifacient; pregnancy must be excluded and prevented. A is dangerous. D and B are false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medication class is metformin?
explain: Correct: B — metformin is a biguanide that reduces hepatic glucose output. D stimulates insulin release. A is injectable hormone. C is a diuretic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which drugs require therapeutic drug monitoring? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, B, E, C — narrow-therapeutic-index drugs need level monitoring. A and F do not routinely.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes montelukast for asthma. Which teaching is correct?
options: Take it daily for prevention, and report mood or behavior changes
Stop it when feeling well, before the end of the shift
It has no side effects, for the duration of the patient's stay
Use it for acute asthma attacks, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — montelukast is daily prevention, not rescue, and carries neuropsychiatric warnings. D misuses it. B invites relapse. C is false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A post-op client is prescribed 1,000 mL of lactated Ringer's over 10 hours through a 20 gtt/mL set. At how many drops per minute should the nurse set the manual infusion?
explain: Correct: D — 1,000/10 = 100 mL/hr; 100 x 20 / 60 = 33.3, or 33 gtt/min. The other options misapply the drop factor.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which medications can cause photosensitivity? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, A, D, B — these drugs heighten sunburn risk; sun protection is needed. E and F do not.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client on linezolid develops agitation and clonus. What should the nurse suspect?
explain: Correct: A — linezolid weakly inhibits MAO and can trigger serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs. B, C, and D miss the emergency.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which over-the-counter pain reliever is safest for a client on warfarin?
explain: Correct: C — acetaminophen does not impair platelets like NSAIDs do. B, A, and D all raise bleeding risk with warfarin.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client with prolonged vomiting has an ABG showing pH 7.53 and bicarbonate 32 mEq/L, with potassium 3.1 mEq/L. Which interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Encourage further vomiting to relieve nausea
explain: Correct: B, C, D, E — vomiting losses cause metabolic alkalosis with hypokalemia; replace potassium, treat the cause with an antiemetic, watch for hypokalemia weakness, and rehydrate orally. F worsens the alkalosis. A would raise bicarbonate further.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which lab value indicates a need for neutropenic precautions?
explain: Correct: B — ANC below 500 signals severe neutropenia. C, A, and D are normal values.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with sepsis has a lactate of 4.5 mmol/L. What does this indicate and what is the priority?
options: Restrict fluids, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Tissue hypoperfusion; give rapid fluids and antibiotics per the sepsis protocol
A normal value; observe, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Give insulin, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B — lactate above 2 signals hypoperfusion; the bundle demands fast fluids, broad-spectrum antibiotics, and source control. C ignores shock. D and A are wrong therapies.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which actions are correct after a myelogram? Select all that apply.
options: Keep the head elevated after the procedure
explain: Correct: D, A, C, E — head elevation, neuro checks, hydration, and prompt reporting of severe headache are standard. B and F are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client has a cystoscopy. Which finding is expected afterward?
options: No urine output for 24 hours, for now
No discomfort at all, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A — pink urine and dysuria are expected after instrumentation. B and D are emergencies. C is unrealistic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are modifiable risk factors for stroke? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, B, F, E — blood pressure control, smoking cessation, diabetes management, and treating afib all lower stroke risk. C and A cannot be changed.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a subarachnoid hemorrhage reports 'the worst headache of my life.' What is the priority?
options: Ambulate the client, at the patient's bedside
Encourage coughing, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Give aspirin, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Maintain a calm, quiet, dark environment; prevent straining; notify the provider stat
explain: Correct: D — prevent rebleed with rest, blood pressure control, and no straining while mobilizing neurosurgery. B raises intracranial pressure. C worsens bleeding. A is dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which are correct blood pressure categories for adults? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, F, B, C — these match current blood pressure categories. A can indicate hypotension. E is stage 2 hypertension.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client is scheduled for an intravenous pyelogram. Which preparation is correct?
options: No preparation is needed, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Restrict all fluids afterward, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
NPO as directed, check for contrast allergy, and encourage fluids afterward
Bowel prep with barium, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: C — NPO, allergy screening, and post-procedure hydration protect the kidneys from contrast. A, D, and B are wrong.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which interventions treat hypovolemic shock? Select all that apply.
options: Vasopressors per orders if fluids fail
Control the source of fluid loss
explain: Correct: F, D, B, C — restore volume, stop the loss, support pressure if needed, and track output. E is outdated and ineffective. A worsens shock.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with GI bleeding has blood pressure 80/50 mmHg, heart rate 130, and confusion. What is the priority?
options: Give a sedative, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care
Give oral fluids, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care
Wait for lab results, which is included in the documentation for the patient's care, at the patient's bedside
Establish large-bore IV access, give isotonic fluids, type and crossmatch, and notify the provider stat
explain: Correct: D — hemorrhagic shock needs immediate vascular access, volume, blood ready, and escalation. B is inadequate. C delays resuscitation. A is dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which value indicates normal serum calcium?
explain: Correct: B — calcium is 8.5-10.5 mg/dL. C is critically low. A is hypercalcemic. D is the magnesium range.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with varicose veins asks about self-care. What should the nurse teach?
options: Avoid all exercise, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Stand in one place all day, while using proper body mechanics to avoid injury
Elevate the legs, wear compression stockings, and avoid prolonged standing
Cross the legs frequently, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C — elevation, compression, movement, and weight control ease venous pooling. B and D worsen it. A causes deconditioning.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are signs of Buerger's disease? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, B, E, D — Buerger's strikes young smokers with claudication, color changes, and digit ischemia; quitting is the key treatment. A describes the wrong population. C is backwards.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with pleurisy has sharp pain when breathing. Which action helps?
options: Splint the chest and take analgesics as ordered
Vigorous deep breathing, on this occasion, for now
Ignore the pain, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A — splinting plus analgesics eases pleuritic pain while the cause is treated. C worsens pain. B is unsafe. D ignores suffering.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which is the most common cause of lung cancer?
explain: Correct: B — smoking causes the large majority of lung cancers. C, D, and A protect against it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with myxedema coma is hypothermic and bradycardic. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: Rapid aggressive warming, for the duration of the patient's stay
An ice bath, in accordance with facility policy
IV levothyroxine with gentle rewarming and corticosteroid support
No treatment, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
explain: Correct: C — myxedema coma needs IV thyroid hormone, slow rewarming (fast warming causes collapse), and steroids for possible adrenal failure. A causes vasodilation and shock. D and B are lethal.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are signs of pheochromocytoma? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: A, E, B, C — catecholamine surges cause paroxysmal hypertension, headache, diaphoresis, and palpitations. F and D are the opposite findings.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with suspected pheochromocytoma needs an abdominal assessment. What should the nurse do?
options: Palpate the abdomen firmly, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Massage the abdomen, in accordance with facility policy
Percuss vigorously, as documented in the plan of care
Avoid abdominal palpation; it can trigger a hypertensive crisis
explain: Correct: D — palpating the tumor releases catecholamines and can precipitate crisis. A, B, and C are all dangerous.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with irritable bowel syndrome asks about the disorder. What should the nurse teach?
options: There is no intestinal inflammation; manage stress and diet triggers
Ignore the symptoms, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Surgery is required, before the end of the shift
It causes permanent intestinal damage, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — IBS is functional without inflammation; stress and diet management help. D describes IBD. C is wrong. B dismisses real distress.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which is the best dietary source of vitamin C?
explain: Correct: C — citrus fruits are rich in vitamin C. D, B, and A are poor sources.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are emergency oncologic complications? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, F, E, B — SVC obstruction, cord compression, tumor lysis, and neutropenic fever are all emergencies. C and A are not.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with superior vena cava syndrome has facial edema and jugular vein distention. What is the priority positioning?
explain: Correct: D — upright positioning reduces venous congestion in the head and neck. C and A worsen edema. B is inappropriate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with cancer develops new back pain with leg weakness. What should the nurse suspect?
explain: Correct: A — back pain plus neuro deficits in cancer means cord compression until proven otherwise; it needs emergency steroids and evaluation. D, B, and C dangerously minimize it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client develops fat embolism syndrome after a femur fracture, with dyspnea, confusion, and petechiae. What is the priority?
options: Ambulate immediately, as documented in the plan of care
Give oxygen, monitor closely, and notify the provider stat
Discharge home, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Massage the leg, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B — fat emboli to lungs and brain need oxygen, close monitoring, and escalation. A and D dislodge more fat. C is unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with a draining wound over the tibia has a suspected bone infection. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Encourage weight bearing on the affected leg
Assess pain, swelling, and warmth at the site
Stop antibiotics once the fever resolves
Obtain wound cultures before antibiotics per orders
explain: Correct: E, B, C, F — cultures guide therapy, ongoing assessment tracks the infection, inflammatory markers show response, and the full IV antibiotic course treats osteomyelitis. A risks pathologic fracture. D causes relapse; treatment runs for weeks.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which organism causes tuberculosis?
explain: Correct: D — Mycobacterium tuberculosis causes TB. A, C, and B cause other infections.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with toxic shock syndrome has fever, rash, and hypotension with prolonged tampon use. What is the priority?
options: Give an antipyretic only, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Remove the tampon, give fluids and antibiotics, and notify the provider stat
Discharge home, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Leave the tampon in place, and wash hands before and after the procedure
explain: Correct: B — remove the toxin source, resuscitate, and treat the staphylococcal infection aggressively. D continues toxin absorption. A and C are inadequate.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which are risk factors for pelvic inflammatory disease? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, A, B, C — partner number, STI history, douching, and young age raise PID risk. E and D protect against it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with endometriosis asks about symptoms. What should the nurse teach?
options: Severe menstrual cramps, pain with intercourse, and possible infertility can occur
It only affects men, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Periods are always painless, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
It never causes symptoms, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: A — ectopic endometrial tissue causes dysmenorrhea, dyspareunia, and infertility. C, D, and B are false.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Four children arrive in the emergency department after a school bus accident. Which child should the nurse assess first?
options: Child crying loudly with a deformed forearm
Child with a small forehead laceration
Child with noisy breathing and drooling
explain: Correct: C — noisy breathing with drooling signals an airway emergency, the top priority. A is a painful fracture but stable. D and B are minor injuries.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which task can the nurse delegate to the UAP for a stable post-op client?
options: Ambulating the client in the hallway
Teaching about medications, at this stage
Assessing the surgical incision, for now
Adjusting the IV rate, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A — ambulating a stable client is a routine UAP task. C, D, and B all require RN judgment or licensure.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions demonstrate client advocacy by the nurse? Select all that apply.
options: Telling the client the provider is always right
Questioning a provider order that conflicts with the client's stated wishes
Agreeing to withhold the diagnosis because the family requests it
Providing information the client requested about treatment options
Arranging an interpreter for a client with limited English
explain: Correct: C, F, E — advocacy means speaking up for the client's wishes, ensuring understanding, and informing. D violates the client's autonomy. B is routine documentation, not advocacy. A dismisses the client's concerns.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client has a do-not-resuscitate order. What is the nurse's responsibility?
options: Ask the family to override it each shift
Ignore the order during an emergency, as documented in the plan of care
Ensure the order is documented and honor the client's wishes
Hide the order from the team, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C — a valid DNR must be visible in the record and honored. B violates autonomy. A is unnecessary and distressing. D endangers the client's wishes.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: During START triage after a building collapse, a victim is apneic even after the airway is opened. Which tag is appropriate?
explain: Correct: B — apnea after airway positioning is expectant in START triage. Red is for salvageable immediate needs. Yellow is delayed. Green is walking wounded.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse suspects a colleague is impaired by alcohol at work. What should the nurse do?
options: Ignore it, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Confront the colleague physically, at this stage
Report the concern to the supervisor per policy
explain: Correct: D — the nurse has a duty to protect clients by reporting impairment through proper channels. C enables danger. B is unsafe. A abandons the duty.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse believes a provider's order is unsafe. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Notify the charge nurse of the concern
Escalate up the chain of command if unresolved
Refuse to carry out any orders from that provider ever again
Question the provider directly about the order
Carry out the order without question
explain: Correct: E, A, B, C — clarify, notify, document, and escalate through the chain of command. D is an overreaction that abandons clients. F carries out a potentially harmful order.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Who is responsible for obtaining informed consent for surgery?
options: The bedside nurse, on this occasion
The UAP, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: A — the provider performing the procedure must obtain consent; the nurse witnesses the signature. B witnesses only. C and D cannot obtain consent.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A medical-surgical nurse is floated to the labor unit. What is the best response?
options: Leave the hospital, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Take a full labor assignment independently, at the patient's bedside
Accept an assignment within competency and request orientation to the unit
Refuse to enter the unit, since the same approach was used during the previous shift
explain: Correct: C — floating is acceptable with an assignment matching competency plus orientation. D refuses without cause. B exceeds safe competency. A is abandonment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which clients should the nurse refer to case management for discharge planning? Select all that apply.
options: Healthy young adult after an uncomplicated appendectomy
Older adult living alone after hip fracture repair
Client with newly diagnosed diabetes needing teaching
Client with well-controlled hypertension going home with family
Client with end-stage COPD on home oxygen
explain: Correct: C, A, D, F — frailty, new ostomy, new complex diagnosis, and home oxygen all need coordinated planning. E and B have strong support and simple needs.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A client falls and is uninjured. What should the nurse do about the incident report?
options: Write 'incident report filed' in the client's chart, on this occasion
Document the facts of the fall in the chart and file a separate incident report
Do not document the fall at all, and delay reassessment until the next scheduled shift
Blame the client in the chart, as part of the routine care for this patient
explain: Correct: B — chart the objective facts; the incident report is a separate quality document never referenced in the chart. A creates legal risk. C omits required documentation. D is unprofessional.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: During team rounds, the RN assigns morning tasks to the LPN. Which task falls within the LPN's scope?
options: Performing the initial admission assessment on a new client
Creating the nursing plan of care
Triaging clients in the emergency department
Administering 0800 oral medications to stable clients
explain: Correct: D — LPNs administer scheduled oral medications to stable clients. A, C, and B require RN assessment and judgment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A nurse is asked to accept an assignment that feels unsafe due to short staffing. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Accept the assignment and document the staffing concern
Work beyond competency without asking questions
Notify the supervisor of the concern
explain: Correct: C, F, D, A — accept without abandoning clients, document, notify, and seek help. B is abandonment. E risks client harm.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Two nurses disagree about a client's care. What is the best first step?
options: Address the concern directly with the nurse involved
Ignore the disagreement, on this occasion, for now
File a grievance immediately, at this stage, in full
Complain to other staff, in practice
explain: Correct: A — direct, respectful communication resolves most conflicts first. D spreads gossip. C skips the direct step. B lets the problem grow.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which post-op client should the nurse see first?
options: Client with controlled pain asking for ice chips, as documented in the plan of care
Client awaiting discharge teaching, based on the findings documented so far
Client with a functioning PCA pump, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Client with a saturated dressing, blood pressure 88/52 mmHg, and restlessness
explain: Correct: D — bleeding with hypotension and restlessness signals hemorrhagic shock. A, B, and C are stable and routine.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: The LPN reports a client's blood pressure is 70/40 mmHg. What should the RN do?
options: Delegate the assessment to the UAP, at the patient's bedside
Go assess the client personally right away
Document the value and move on
Tell the LPN to recheck in 4 hours
explain: Correct: B — severe hypotension needs immediate RN assessment; assessment of an unstable client cannot be delegated. D delays care. A delegates assessment improperly. C ignores a crisis.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: During a busy shift, several situations arise. In which situations must the RN personally reassess the client rather than relying on UAP or LPN data? Select all that apply.
options: The LPN reports a blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg
The UAP reports the client fell
Routine vital signs are stable and unchanged
The client requests as-needed pain medication
A stable client asks for an extra blanket
The UAP reports the client has new chest pain
explain: Correct: F, A, B, D — new chest pain, severe hypotension, a fall, and a PRN medication request all need RN assessment and judgment. C and E are routine and stable.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which information is most important when handing off a client to the home health nurse?
options: The client's favorite television shows, before the end of the shift
The client's old room number, as documented in the plan of care
Medication list, allergies, and pending wound care needs
The nurse's personal opinion of the family, during the current shift
explain: Correct: C — medications, allergies, and ongoing care needs ensure safe continuity. A, D, and B do not affect care.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which best defines a sentinel event?
options: A minor documentation error, on this occasion
A routine near miss, as documented in the plan of care
An unexpected event causing serious harm or death
A scheduled procedure, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C — sentinel events cause death or major permanent harm and trigger investigation. B, D, and A do not meet the definition.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which are quality improvement activities? Select all that apply.
options: Hiding errors to protect the unit
explain: Correct: A, C, F, B — measuring outcomes, analyzing causes, comparing to standards, and gathering client feedback improve care. E and D create fear and hide problems.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: A mercury thermometer breaks on the unit floor. What should the nurse do?
options: Keep people away and notify environmental services for hazmat cleanup
Mop it with hot water, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Vacuum up the mercury, on this occasion, for now
Sweep it into the trash, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A — mercury needs hazmat cleanup; vacuuming spreads toxic vapor. C spreads contamination. D and B expose staff and clients.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Before a client enters the MRI suite, what must the nurse verify?
options: No screening is needed, in accordance with facility policy
The client is wearing jewelry, during the current shift
The client ate a full meal, at the patient's bedside
No metal implants, devices, or objects are present
explain: Correct: D — MRI magnets make metal implants and objects dangerous; screening is mandatory. C is irrelevant. B is dangerous. A skips safety.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which precautions are correct for a client with a latex allergy? Select all that apply.
options: Post a latex allergy alert sign
Schedule the procedure as the first case of the day
Avoid latex balloons and rubber products in the room
explain: Correct: D, F, E, B — latex-free supplies, removing latex sources, first-case scheduling to reduce airborne particles, and clear alerts protect the client. A ignores a life-threatening allergy. C exposes the client to latex.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A nurse finds an IV pump with a frayed electrical cord. What should the nurse do?
options: Plug it into a different outlet, in accordance with facility policy
Remove the pump from service, tag it, and report it to maintenance
Use it only for stable clients, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Tape the cord and keep using the pump, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: B — damaged cords are shock and fire hazards; remove, tag, and report. D, C, and A keep a dangerous device in use.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A parent asks about car seat safety for a 1-year-old. What should the nurse teach?
options: Use a seat belt alone, before the end of the shift
Hold the child on an adult's lap, at the patient's bedside
Face forward in the front seat, while using proper body mechanics to avoid injury
Keep rear-facing in the back seat as long as possible, at least to age 2
explain: Correct: D — rear-facing in the back seat protects the head and spine; keep it as long as the seat allows, minimum to age 2. C, A, and B greatly increase injury risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A toddler ingests an unknown household substance. What is the best first action?
options: Wait for symptoms to appear, before the end of the shift
Call poison control and follow their directions
Induce vomiting immediately, on this occasion
Give milk to dilute it, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B — poison control gives substance-specific guidance; vomiting can cause more harm. C can re-injure the esophagus. D is not universally safe. A wastes treatment time.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which teaching points help prevent childhood drowning? Select all that apply.
options: Never leave a child unattended near water
Rely on inflatable floaties for safety
Let children swim alone once they take lessons
Install pool fencing with a locked gate
explain: Correct: A, E, F, C — supervision, CPR skills, barriers, and emptying small pools prevent drowning. B gives false security. D removes the critical supervision layer.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is the most effective basic fall prevention measure for an older adult client?
options: Keep the call light within reach
Remove the call light, for now
Leave the bed in high position
explain: Correct: A — an accessible call light lets the client ask for help instead of getting up alone. C, D, and B all increase fall risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A tornado warning is issued while clients are on the unit. What should the nurse do?
options: Move clients next to the windows to watch, during the current shift
Move clients to interior hallways away from windows
Open all the windows, before the end of the shift
explain: Correct: C — interior spaces away from glass protect against flying debris. B and D expose clients to shattering glass. A moves them into the storm's path.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which principles protect staff from radiation exposure?
options: Maximize time near the source, during the current shift
Remove the dosimeter badge, in this case
Minimize time, maximize distance, and use shielding
Stand as close as possible, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: C — time, distance, and shielding (ALARA) plus dosimeter monitoring limit exposure. A and D increase it. B removes monitoring.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which practices demonstrate correct sharps safety? Select all that apply.
options: Carry used sharps in a uniform pocket
Never recap needles with two hands
Fill sharps containers above the fill line
Dispose of sharps in a puncture-resistant container
explain: Correct: E, B, F — proper containers, no two-handed recapping, and safety devices prevent needlesticks. D causes sticks. C risks overflow injury. A endangers everyone.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: How should look-alike sound-alike medications be stored?
options: Without any labels, in accordance with facility policy
Separately with tall-man lettering and alerts
Side by side alphabetically, on this occasion
Mixed together in one bin, at this stage, for now
explain: Correct: B — separation plus tall-man lettering (e.g., hydrALAZINE vs hydrOXYzine) prevents mix-ups. C, D, and A invite errors.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which is an expected milestone for a 9-month-old infant?
options: Reads simple words, at this stage
Rides a bicycle, in accordance with facility policy
Uses a pincer grasp and babbles 'mama' or 'dada'
explain: Correct: D — pincer grasp and canonical babbling emerge around 9 months. B, A, and C are years beyond this age.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which health promotion topics are appropriate for an adolescent visit? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, E, D, B — vaccines, mental health screening, injury prevention, and activity are adolescent priorities. A and C harm health.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A school-age child rides a bicycle daily. What should the nurse teach?
options: Wear a properly fitted helmet on every ride
No helmet is needed on sidewalks, in full
Helmets are only for long rides, in practice
explain: Correct: A — a fitted helmet every ride prevents head injury. D, B, and C all increase injury risk.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A woman is planning pregnancy. Which supplement should the nurse recommend?
explain: Correct: B — folic acid before conception prevents neural tube defects. D alone is insufficient. A is teratogenic in excess. C misses a proven prevention.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which exercise best reduces fall risk in older adults?
options: High-impact running only, at this stage
Prolonged bed rest, during the current shift
No exercise at all, for now
Tai chi with balance and strength training
explain: Correct: D — tai chi plus strength and balance work improves stability. C and B cause deconditioning. A risks injury in frail adults.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which strategies support smoking cessation? Select all that apply.
options: Aim to simply smoke fewer cigarettes
explain: Correct: D, C, E, A — a quit date, NRT, trigger planning, and counseling support quitting. F rejects proven help. B keeps the addiction going.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: An older adult wears dentures. What should the nurse teach about oral health?
options: Remove dentures nightly, clean them, and keep regular dental visits
Clean dentures with bleach daily, as documented in the plan of care
Never remove the dentures, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Dental visits are unnecessary with dentures, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: A — nightly removal, gentle cleaning, and dental checks protect gums and fit. C risks infection. B damages dentures and tissues. D misses oral cancer screening.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: When should Tdap be given in pregnancy?
options: Never during pregnancy, on this occasion
Only after delivery, as documented in the plan of care
During each pregnancy, ideally at 27 to 36 weeks
explain: Correct: C — Tdap each pregnancy at 27-36 weeks passes pertussis protection to the newborn. A and B leave the infant unprotected. D is not the recommended window.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: Which response best demonstrates therapeutic communication?
options: 'Everything will be fine.', in accordance with facility policy
'Why did you do that?', at the patient's bedside
'Tell me more about what you are feeling.'
