explain: Correct: C — open-ended exploration invites the client to share. B demands justification. D judges feelings. A offers false reassurance.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client is experiencing mild anxiety before a procedure. Which nursing actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Place the client in a crowded, noisy dayroom
Guide the client through imagery exercises
Help the client identify coping strategies
explain: Correct: F, D, A, E — expression, imagery, breathing, and coping skills reduce mild anxiety. C overstimulates. B worsens anxiety.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with obsessive-compulsive disorder spends an hour on handwashing rituals. What is the best nursing approach?
options: Ridicule the behavior, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Forcibly stop the ritual, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Ignore the client completely, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Allow time for the ritual while gradually setting limits and offering alternatives
explain: Correct: D — abrupt interruption spikes anxiety; gradual limits with alternatives work. B causes panic. A is abusive. C abandons the client.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with PTSD feels a flashback starting. Which technique should the nurse teach?
options: Grounding: name 5 things you see, 4 you hear, and so on
Relive the trauma in detail alone, before the end of the shift
Avoid all reminders forever, in accordance with facility policy
Use alcohol to calm down, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — sensory grounding anchors the client in the present. B without support can retraumatize. D is maladaptive. C maintains avoidance.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: The parents of an adolescent with anorexia nervosa ask how to support recovery at home. Which teaching points are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Allow the teen to eat alone in the bedroom
Model healthy attitudes toward food and body image
Weigh the teen several times a day
Watch for secret exercising or purging behaviors
Avoid focusing conversations on food, calories, or weight
explain: Correct: A, F, E, C — structured family meals, de-emphasizing food talk, monitoring for behaviors, and healthy modeling support recovery. B enables disordered behaviors in isolation. D fuels obsessive fixation on weight.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client in a manic episode is hyperactive and intrusive on the unit. What is the best milieu approach?
options: Encourage competitive games, as documented in the plan of care
Reduce stimulation, offer a quiet space and finger foods
Engage in lengthy debates, on this occasion
Place the client in a busy group activity
explain: Correct: B — low stimulation, quiet space, and easy-to-eat foods match the manic client's needs. D, C, and A escalate agitation.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: A client with advanced dementia insists a deceased spouse is visiting. What is the best response?
options: Laugh at the confusion, as documented in the plan of care
Argue that the spouse is dead, during the current shift, for now
Use validation: acknowledge the feelings behind the statement
Restrain the client, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C — validation honors the emotion without cruel confrontation. B causes distress. D is unwarranted. A is demeaning.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which are priorities in crisis intervention? Select all that apply.
options: Explore long-term life goals in depth
explain: Correct: C, A, B, E — safety, lethality assessment, rapport, and supports come first in a crisis. F is for later, stable work. D withholds help unfairly.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: An older adult has urge urinary incontinence. Which intervention is best?
options: Prompted voiding on a regular schedule
Fluid restriction all day, for now
explain: Correct: A — scheduled prompted voiding retrains the bladder without catheter risks. D invites infection. C causes dehydration. B gives up on a treatable problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client has constipation. Which measures should the nurse recommend?
options: Daily laxative dependence, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Prolonged bed rest, before the end of the shift, for now
Ignoring the urge to defecate, in accordance with facility policy
High-fiber diet, adequate fluids, and regular activity
explain: Correct: D — fiber, fluids, and movement prevent and treat constipation. B worsens it. C trains the bowel to ignore signals. A creates dependence.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client had spinal surgery and must be turned. Which technique is correct?
options: Twist the client at the waist, during the current shift
Logroll the client keeping the spine straight
Sit the client upright quickly, at the patient's bedside
Pull the client by the arms, in practice
explain: Correct: B — logrolling keeps spinal alignment after spinal surgery. A twists the surgical site. C and D risk injury.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client has non-blanching redness over both heels. Which immediate interventions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Assess the skin with each repositioning
explain: Correct: E, B, A, D — offloading, frequent turns, protective devices, and ongoing skin checks halt a suspected deep tissue injury. C damages fragile tissue. F neglects a deteriorating finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client has a new colostomy. When should the pouch be emptied?
options: When it is one-third to one-half full
Never empty it, on this occasion
Only once a day, at this stage, in practice
explain: Correct: A — emptying at one-third to one-half full prevents leaks and seal breaks. D risks overfilling. B causes leaks and skin damage. C is impossible.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client is receiving continuous enteral feedings. Which action best prevents aspiration?
options: Check placement once a week and document the outcome in the patient's medical record
Keep the client flat at all times, as documented in the plan of care
Give the feeding as fast as possible
Keep the head of the bed elevated 30 to 45 degrees during and after feeding
explain: Correct: D — elevation during and after feeding keeps formula out of the airway. B invites aspiration. C causes intolerance. A misses displacement.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: A client reports a new whistling sound from the hearing aid. What should the nurse do first?
options: Ignore the sound, during the current shift, for now
Remove and reinsert the aid, checking fit and for earwax buildup
Turn the volume to maximum, before the end of the shift
Throw the hearing aid away, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: B — whistling is feedback from poor fit or wax; refit and check the ear. C worsens feedback. D wastes a working device. A ignores the problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: Which actions are correct for denture care? Select all that apply.
options: Soak dentures in water or denture solution when out
Label dentures with the client's name
Clean dentures with very hot water
Handle dentures over a towel or basin of water
Keep dentures in the mouth at all times
Brush dentures with a soft brush
explain: Correct: F, A, B, D — gentle brushing, soaking, labeling, and safe handling protect dentures and gums. E risks gum infection; gums need rest. C warps the plastic.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Basic Care and Comfort

q: The provider prescribes a weight-based heparin infusion of 12 units/kg/hour for a 70-kg client with a pulmonary embolism. The pharmacy sends heparin 25,000 units in 250 mL of D5W. What pump rate in mL/hr delivers the ordered dose?
explain: Correct: C — 12 x 70 = 840 units/hr; concentration 25,000/250 = 100 units/mL; 840/100 = 8.4 mL/hr. The other options double or halve the dose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Order: acetaminophen 15 mg/kg for a child weighing 20 kg. How many mg should the nurse give?
explain: Correct: B — 15 x 20 = 300 mg. A, C, and D miscalculate the weight-based dose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client needs 500 mL of normal saline over 4 hours. The tubing delivers 10 gtt/mL. What manual drip rate in gtt/min should the nurse use?
explain: Correct: C — 500/4 = 125 mL/hr; 125 x 10 / 60 = 20.8, or 21 gtt/min. The other options misapply the drop factor.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which statements about acetaminophen overdose are correct? Select all that apply.
options: Check the acetaminophen level about 4 hours after ingestion
Activated charcoal may help if given early
Inducing vomiting is the best treatment
explain: Correct: E, C, D, B — acetylcysteine restores glutathione, the 4-hour level guides treatment on the nomogram, early charcoal limits absorption, and hepatic necrosis is the danger. F risks aspiration. A ignores a potentially fatal overdose.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client on an ACE inhibitor develops a persistent dry cough. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: Double the ACE inhibitor dose, for now
Add another ACE inhibitor, in this case
Stop all blood pressure treatment, at the patient's bedside
Switch to an angiotensin receptor blocker
explain: Correct: D — ACE inhibitor cough is a classic side effect; ARBs rarely cause it. A worsens the cough. C abandons needed therapy. B doubles the problem.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client wants to stop metoprolol abruptly because of feeling better. What should the nurse teach?
options: Taper as prescribed; abrupt stopping can cause rebound hypertension and chest pain
Stop it suddenly; it is safe, and assess the patient's understanding of the teaching provided
Switch to another drug on your own, for the duration of the patient's stay
Double the dose first, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A — abrupt beta-blocker withdrawal triggers rebound tachycardia, hypertension, and angina. B is dangerous. D and C are unsafe self-adjustments.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which safety measures apply when a client receives IV opioids? Select all that apply.
options: Monitor respiratory rate and sedation level
Assess pain and sedation with each dose
explain: Correct: A, E, F, D — watch for respiratory depression, have the reversal agent ready, prevent atelectasis, and assess response. C dangerously deepens sedation. B risks a fall while sedated.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client on insulin is sweaty, shaky, and confused. What is the priority action?
options: Ignore the symptoms, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Give the next insulin dose, in accordance with facility policy
Have the client drive home, and wash hands before and after the procedure
Give 15 g of fast-acting carbohydrate and recheck glucose in 15 minutes
explain: Correct: D — the rule of 15 treats hypoglycemia quickly. B worsens it. C endangers everyone. A risks seizure or coma.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Before giving digoxin, the nurse finds an apical pulse of 52 beats/min. What should the nurse do?
options: Hold the dose and notify the provider
Give the digoxin as ordered, for now
Double the dose, at the patient's bedside
Give it with an extra dose, during the current shift
explain: Correct: A — hold digoxin for a pulse below 60 and notify the provider; bradycardia signals toxicity risk. B risks dangerous bradycardia. C and D are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which teaching points are correct for a client starting lithium? Select all that apply.
options: Keep salt and fluid intake consistent
Report increased thirst, tremor, or diarrhea
Have lithium levels monitored as ordered
Stay well hydrated, especially in heat
explain: Correct: A, C, B, E — steady sodium and fluids stabilize levels, monitoring catches toxicity, early symptoms need reporting, and hydration protects the kidneys. F concentrates lithium dangerously. D raises lithium levels.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client takes clozapine. Which laboratory monitoring is essential?
options: Urine culture weekly, on this occasion, for now
No labs are needed, in accordance with facility policy
Weekly blood glucose only, in full
explain: Correct: B — clozapine can cause fatal agranulocytosis; ANC monitoring is mandatory. D alone misses the key risk. C and A ignore it.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client on sertraline develops hyperthermia, clonus, and agitation after starting tramadol. What should the nurse suspect?
explain: Correct: C — SSRI plus tramadol triggered serotonin excess: hyperthermia, clonus, and mental status change. A, B, and D miss a life-threatening emergency.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which safety measures apply during heparin infusion therapy? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: F, D, B, C — aPTT guides dosing, platelet drops signal HIT, and avoiding IM sticks and blade razors prevents bleeding. A adds bleeding risk. E can cause rebound clotting.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: A client of childbearing age is prescribed isotretinoin for acne. Which teaching is essential?
options: Take it only when pregnant, before the end of the shift
It is safe during pregnancy, within the scope of the practical nurse's role
No precautions are needed, on this occasion, for now
It is teratogenic; use strict contraception and pregnancy testing
explain: Correct: D — isotretinoin causes severe birth defects; pregnancy must be prevented and tested for. B and A are dangerous. C ignores the risk.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies

q: Which items belong on the pre-op checklist before general anesthesia?
options: NPO status, allergies, signed consent, and removal of dentures and jewelry
Keep all metal jewelry on, in accordance with facility policy
No verification is needed, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Full meal just before surgery, as documented in the plan of care
explain: Correct: A — NPO prevents aspiration; allergy and consent verification plus removing dentures and jewelry are standard. D risks aspiration. C and B skip safety.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which findings suggest deep vein thrombosis? Select all that apply.
options: A positive Homans' sign confirms DVT
Warmth and redness of the leg
explain: Correct: F, C, E, A — unilateral pain, swelling, warmth, and sudden dyspnea (possible pulmonary embolism) fit venous thromboembolism. D is wrong — Homans' sign is unreliable. B describes arterial insufficiency.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which laboratory test is most specific for myocardial infarction?
explain: Correct: C — troponin is the most specific marker of cardiac muscle injury. A, B, and D do not diagnose MI.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which discharge instruction is most important after a colonoscopy with conscious sedation and polyp removal?
options: Drink alcohol to relax, before the end of the shift, for now
Have a responsible adult drive you home and rest for the day
Operate machinery this evening, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Drive yourself home, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B — sedation impairs judgment and reflexes for 24 hours; a driver and rest are required. D and C risk injury. A interacts with sedation.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client with a COPD exacerbation has ABG: pH 7.30, PaCO2 58 mmHg, HCO3 26 mEq/L. Which imbalance is present?
explain: Correct: D — low pH with high PaCO2 is respiratory acidosis from CO2 retention. B, C, and A misread the values.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: During a blood transfusion, the client develops itching, hives, and wheezing. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Give the next unit, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Stop the transfusion, keep the IV open with normal saline, and notify the provider
Slow the transfusion rate, as documented in the plan of care
Document and continue, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B — stop the blood, maintain access with saline, and escalate; this looks like an allergic/anaphylactic reaction. C continues the exposure. A and D endanger the client.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which precautions are correct when removing a central venous catheter? Select all that apply.
options: Remove the catheter during deep inspiration
Instruct the client to hold the breath or bear down
Occlude the site immediately upon removal
Position the client flat or in slight Trendelenburg
Have the client cough vigorously during removal
explain: Correct: E, C, D, A — flat or head-down positioning, breath-holding or Valsalva, immediate occlusion, and pressure prevent air embolism. F and B increase negative intrathoracic pressure and air entry.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Six hours after a lumbar puncture, the client reports a severe headache that worsens when sitting up. What should the nurse do?
options: Keep the client flat, encourage fluids, and notify the provider
Have the client sit upright in a chair, as documented in the plan of care
Restrict all fluids, on this occasion
Encourage vigorous exercise, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: A — a post-dural-puncture headache improves lying flat with hydration; notify the provider for possible further treatment. B worsens it. D and C are unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: How should the nurse position a client for a thoracentesis?
options: Lying flat on the back, before the end of the shift
Sitting upright leaning forward over a table
Lying on the stomach, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: C — sitting and leaning forward spreads the ribs and widens access to the pleural space. A, D, and B are incorrect positions.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Before a paracentesis, what should the nurse instruct the client to do?
options: Drink a large amount of water
explain: Correct: B — an empty bladder avoids puncture during needle insertion. D fills the bladder dangerously. C is unnecessary. A is irrelevant.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: Which nursing actions are correct after a cardiac catheterization via the femoral artery? Select all that apply.
options: Remove the pressure dressing right away
Monitor the site for bleeding or hematoma
Check pulses distal to the insertion site
Keep the affected leg straight with bed rest as ordered
explain: Correct: E, D, F, B — distal pulses detect arterial compromise, site checks catch bleeding, immobilization prevents hemorrhage, and chest pain monitoring catches complications. A risks bleeding. C removes needed pressure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: How should a client prepare for an EEG?
options: Arrive with clean, dry hair and avoid caffeine and stimulants
Drink several cups of coffee beforehand, during the current shift
Stay awake for 3 days straight, based on the findings documented so far
Use lots of hair oil, and wash hands before and after the procedure
explain: Correct: A — clean hair ensures electrode contact; caffeine and stimulants distort brain waves. B alters the tracing. D blocks contact. C is excessive and unsafe.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Reduction of Risk Potential

q: A client has crushing chest pain suspected to be MI. What is the nurse's first action?
options: Give an antacid, during the current shift, for now
Have the client walk it off, and verify the order against the medication administration record
Give chewable aspirin per protocol, obtain vitals and EKG, and notify the provider stat
Wait 30 minutes to see if it passes, while observing standard isolation precautions for the unit
explain: Correct: C — aspirin, rapid EKG, and escalation save heart muscle; time is critical. D wastes the reperfusion window. A misdiagnoses. B increases oxygen demand.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings suggest myocardial infarction rather than stable angina? Select all that apply.
options: Pain unrelieved by rest or nitroglycerin
Diaphoresis and nausea with the pain
Pain relieved within minutes by rest
explain: Correct: A, D, C, B — prolonged unrelieved pain, troponin rise, ST elevation, and autonomic symptoms mark infarction. F and E describe stable angina.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with atrial fibrillation has a heart rate of 150 beats/min and is stable. What should the nurse anticipate?
options: Cough vigorously, at the patient's bedside
No treatment is needed, during the current shift, for now
Immediate defibrillation, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Rate control with a beta blocker or calcium channel blocker per orders
explain: Correct: D — stable rapid afib needs rate control first. C is for unstable or lethal rhythms. B ignores the rapid rate. A is not a treatment.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings suggest pacemaker malfunction?
options: Feeling energetic, based on the findings documented so far
Regular pulse at the set rate, as documented in the plan of care
Pulse rate matching the set rate, before the end of the shift
Dizziness, hiccups, and a pulse slower than the set rate
explain: Correct: D — failure to capture or sense causes bradycardia symptoms like dizziness and diaphragmatic hiccups. C, A, and B describe normal function.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings are associated with infective endocarditis?
options: Osler nodes, Janeway lesions, and a new heart murmur with fever
Clear lungs and no fever, then reassess the patient after the intervention
Normal heart sounds always, for now
No skin findings ever, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A — painful Osler nodes, painless Janeway lesions, new murmur, and fever are classic. B, C, and D deny the characteristic findings.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings are characteristic of pericarditis? Select all that apply.
options: Chest pain relieved by sitting upright and leaning forward
Severe shortness of breath only when running
Pain that worsens when lying flat
explain: Correct: A, B, E, F — positional relief leaning forward, friction rub, diffuse ST elevation, and worse pain supine are classic pericarditis. C describes reflux. D is too narrow.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with severe COPD develops right-sided heart failure. What is this called and what is the priority?
options: Normal aging; no action needed, during the current shift, for now
Cardiomyopathy; restrict all activity, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Cor pulmonale; optimize oxygenation and monitor respiratory status
Left heart failure; give fluids rapidly, in full
explain: Correct: C — cor pulmonale is right heart failure from lung disease; oxygenation and respiratory monitoring are key. D misidentifies the side. B is the wrong diagnosis. A ignores failure.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with rib fractures has paradoxical chest movement. What does the nurse suspect?
explain: Correct: B — paradoxical movement (segment moves in on inspiration) defines flail chest. C, D, and A do not cause this finding.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with a chest tube suddenly develops tracheal deviation, jugular vein distention, and hypotension. What should the nurse do?
options: Increase the suction, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Clamp the chest tube, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Reassure the client and wait, as documented in the plan of care
Notify the provider stat; prepare for needle decompression of a tension pneumothorax
explain: Correct: D — tracheal deviation with JVD and hypotension is tension pneumothorax, a lethal emergency needing immediate decompression. B worsens it. A does not fix tension. C wastes critical minutes.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which actions are correct during an acute asthma exacerbation? Select all that apply.
options: Expect the client to speak in full sentences
explain: Correct: B, F, A, E — albuterol opens airways first, upright positioning aids breathing, oxygen corrects hypoxia, and peak flow tracks response. C is wrong — short phrases signal severe obstruction. D worsens breathing.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A child with cystic fibrosis asks why daily chest physiotherapy is needed. What should the nurse explain?
options: It is just for exercise, as part of the patient's ongoing care
It loosens thick mucus so it can be coughed out, preventing lung infections
It cures the disease, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
It is optional, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B — airway clearance removes the thick secretions that breed infection. A understates its purpose. C overpromises. D risks serious infection.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client shows facial droop, arm drift, and slurred speech starting 2 hours ago. What is the priority?
options: Activate the stroke protocol; the client may be eligible for thrombolytics within 4.5 hours
Give aspirin and send home, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Check blood sugar next week, as documented in the plan of care
Wait until tomorrow, as listed among the options in the patient's current plan of care, for now
explain: Correct: A — FAST symptoms within the window demand immediate stroke protocol and tPA evaluation. D wastes brain. B skips needed workup. C delays care.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client is in status epilepticus. Which medication should the nurse anticipate first?
explain: Correct: C — IV lorazepam is first-line to stop prolonged seizures. B and D are too slow orally. A is irrelevant.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings support a diagnosis of bacterial meningitis? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: D, B, E, A — neck stiffness, Kernig's and Brudzinski's signs, and photophobia are classic meningeal signs. C is wrong — fever is common but its absence does not rule out meningitis.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with Guillain-Barré syndrome has ascending weakness. What is the nursing priority?
options: Encourage marathon walking, on this occasion
explain: Correct: B — ascending paralysis can reach respiratory muscles; watch vital capacity and prepare for ventilation. D is unsafe. C and A ignore a life-threatening progression.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with myasthenia gravis has ptosis and diplopia that worsen with activity. Which test confirms the diagnosis?
options: Chest X-ray alone, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Urinalysis, for the duration of the patient's stay
Fasting blood glucose, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: C — edrophonium briefly improves myasthenic weakness, confirming the diagnosis. D, A, and B do not test neuromuscular transmission.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Which findings are characteristic of Parkinson's disease? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: C, A, F, B — shuffling steps, resting pill-rolling tremor, slowed movement, and rigidity form the classic tetrad. E is false — there is no cure. D describes Huntington's chorea.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: A client with multiple sclerosis asks about hot baths. What should the nurse teach?
options: Heat can temporarily worsen symptoms; avoid hot baths and overheating
Heat improves all symptoms, on this occasion
Temperature has no effect, at this stage
Take very hot baths daily, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: A — elevated temperature transiently worsens MS symptoms (Uhthoff's phenomenon). B and D invite symptom flares. C denies a well-known effect.
domain: Physiological Integrity: Physiological Adaptation

q: Four burn clients arrive after a house fire. Which client should the nurse assess first?
options: Client with a small first-degree sunburn, for now
Client with a minor scald awaiting discharge
Client with healed skin grafts, before the end of the shift
Client with 45% total body surface area partial-thickness burns
explain: Correct: D — extensive partial-thickness burns risk airway compromise, shock, and fluid loss. A, C, and B are minor or resolved.

q: The RN is assigning tasks to the UAP for the shift. Which assignment is appropriate?
options: Assess a newly admitted client's pain
Teach a client to use the incentive spirometer
Record intake and output for stable clients
Titrate oxygen for a client in respiratory distress
explain: Correct: C — recording I&O for stable clients is routine UAP work. D, A, and B require RN judgment and assessment.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which actions reflect the ethical principle of fidelity in nursing? Select all that apply.
options: Documenting care that was not given
Lying to the client to avoid conflict
explain: Correct: D, C, B — fidelity means keeping promises, following through, and staying competent. F breaks the commitment. A is fraud. E violates honesty.

q: A client is a potential organ donor. Who should approach the family about donation?
explain: Correct: A — trained designated requestors approach families to protect the process and the grieving family. B alone is not the standard. D and C are inappropriate.

q: A suspicious package is found on the unit. What should the nurse do first?
options: Open the package to inspect it, while maintaining standard precautions throughout
Shake the package to hear its contents, during the current shift
Ignore it, according to the documentation maintained for the patient's care, for now
Notify security and evacuate per policy without touching the package

q: A nurse suspects a child is being abused. What is the nurse's legal duty?
options: Prove the abuse before acting, at the patient's bedside
Report the suspicion to child protective services
Confront the parents aggressively, at this stage
Document nothing, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B — nurses are mandatory reporters; suspicion alone triggers the report. A is not required. C is unsafe. D violates the duty.

q: Which activities are within the RN scope of practice? Select all that apply.
options: Developing the nursing plan of care
Prescribing medications independently as an RN
explain: Correct: A, E, C — nursing diagnosis, teaching, and care planning are RN functions. B is the provider's role. F requires advanced practice licensure. D is restricted by setting and law.

q: An emancipated minor needs treatment. Who can give consent?
explain: Correct: D — emancipated minors consent for their own care. A is unnecessary. C has no authority. B is false.

q: A client who is a Jehovah's Witness refuses blood transfusion before surgery. What should the nurse do?
options: Cancel all care, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Respect the refusal and discuss bloodless alternatives with the team
Transfuse anyway, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Have the family override the decision, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: B — a competent adult's refusal stands; bloodless techniques and volume expanders are alternatives. C violates autonomy. D cannot override a competent adult. A abandons the client.

q: Which referrals help prevent heart failure readmissions? Select all that apply.
options: Instructions to avoid all physical activity
explain: Correct: A, C, F, B — home monitoring, diet teaching, rehab, and med review prevent decompensation. E abandons follow-up. D causes deconditioning; activity is prescribed.

q: The nurse forgot to chart a medication given 2 hours ago. What is the correct action?
options: Chart a 'late entry' with the current date and time
Chart it under another nurse's name
Backdate the entry to the original time
Skip the documentation, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A — a late entry with the current date and time is honest and legal. C falsifies the record. D omits required documentation. B is fraud.

q: Which wound care task can the nurse delegate to the LPN?
options: Debriding necrotic tissue, before the end of the shift, for now
Sterile dressing change on a stable wound per orders
Initial assessment of a new wound, during the current shift

q: Which statements about floating to another unit are correct? Select all that apply.
options: The nurse is entitled to orientation to the new unit
The nurse must accept any assignment without question
The nurse should clarify expectations with the charge nurse
The nurse may abandon the assignment if unhappy
The nurse must perform tasks beyond legal scope
The nurse may refuse only if the assignment is beyond competency
explain: Correct: F, A, C — refuse only beyond competency, get oriented, and clarify expectations. B ignores competency limits. D is abandonment. E violates the nurse practice act.

q: A nurse experiences lateral violence from a coworker. What is the best response?
options: Accept it as normal, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Address it directly or report it through proper channels
Retaliate in kind, on this occasion
Quit without notice, as it appears in the orders written for this patient

q: The nurse is caring for four laboring clients. Which needs immediate intervention?
options: Client with a prolapsed umbilical cord and fetal bradycardia
Client resting comfortably after an epidural with blood pressure 110/70 mmHg
Client awaiting an epidural who is stable
Client in early labor coping well

q: What is the preceptor's role with a newly graduated RN?
options: Assign only the hardest clients, for now
Do all the work for the new nurse, during the current shift
Guide, support, and evaluate the new nurse's practice
Ignore the new nurse, for the duration of the patient's stay
explain: Correct: C — precepting means guided supervision with feedback. B prevents learning. D abandons support. A overwhelms the novice.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Management of Care

q: Which elements belong in an SBAR handoff? Select all that apply.
explain: Correct: E, D, B, F — Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation structure safe handoffs. C and A are unprofessional and irrelevant.

q: The unit's fall rate has risen for 3 months. What should the nurse do first?
options: Ignore the trend, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Hide the data, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Blame the night shift, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Investigate causes and implement targeted prevention strategies
explain: Correct: D — trending data drives investigation and improvement. A, C, and B avoid the quality duty.

q: When resources are scarce, how should the nurse participate in allocation decisions?
options: By personal preference, on this occasion, for now
By likelihood of benefit using fair, established criteria
By the client's social worth, before the end of the shift
By who arrived last, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: B — justice requires fair criteria based on need and likely benefit. C, A, and D are discriminatory or arbitrary.

q: Which actions could constitute false imprisonment? Select all that apply.
options: Keeping a client at the family's request against the client's will
Applying restraints without a provider order
Preventing a competent client from leaving against medical advice
Detaining a client for an unpaid bill
explain: Correct: B, D, F, A — restraining without order, blocking AMA departure, detaining for payment, and holding for family convenience all unlawfully confine. E is consensual. C is legally authorized.

q: After a suspected inhalation anthrax exposure, which prophylaxis is given?

q: A chemical spill occurs in the hallway. What should the nurse do?
options: Evacuate the area moving upwind and notify the response team
Taste the chemical to identify it, during the current shift
Mop it up barehanded, at the patient's bedside
Walk through the spill quickly, as part of the patient's ongoing care
explain: Correct: A — move upwind to avoid vapors, evacuate others, and call hazmat. D, B, and C risk toxic exposure.

q: Which are correct seizure precautions? Select all that apply.

Keep the bed in the lowest position
Place a tongue blade in the mouth
Keep suction and oxygen at the bedside
explain: Correct: B, F, E, C — padded rails, rescue equipment, supervision, and low bed position protect the client. A causes injury. D damages teeth and blocks the airway.

q: A new parent asks about safe infant sleep. What should the nurse teach?
options: Use a soft mattress with stuffed animals
Share the bed with heavy blankets, before administering any further medication
Place the infant on the stomach with pillows, as documented in the plan of care
Place the infant on the back on a firm mattress with no soft bedding
explain: Correct: D — back to sleep on a firm, bare surface prevents SIDS and suffocation. C, B, and A all increase risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which playground features are safest for young children?
options: Concrete surfacing under equipment, for now
Shock-absorbing surfacing, age-appropriate equipment, and adult supervision
No supervision needed, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Broken equipment, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: B — soft surfacing, right-sized equipment, and supervision prevent injuries. A, D, and C invite harm.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A family has a firearm at home with children present. What should the nurse teach?
options: Children do not need any teaching about guns
Hide the loaded gun under a pillow, as part of the patient's ongoing care
Keep the loaded gun within reach, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Store the firearm unloaded and locked, with ammunition locked separately
explain: Correct: D — unloaded, locked storage with ammunition separate prevents tragedies. C and B invite accidental shootings. A misses critical safety teaching.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which teaching points are correct for flood safety? Select all that apply.
options: Floodwater is safe when it looks clear
Stay away from downed power lines
Re-enter the home only when officials say it is safe
Drink floodwater if it looks clear
explain: Correct: C, B, D, E — floodwater hides contamination and currents, cars stall or wash away, power lines electrify water, and structures may be unsafe. F and A risk infection and injury.

q: During a heat wave, how should an older adult stay safe?
options: Avoid all fluids, as recorded in the patient's chart for the current admission
Exercise vigorously at midday, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Stay hydrated, remain in cool environments, and have someone check in regularly
Stay in a hot attic, and encourage the patient to report any new symptoms
explain: Correct: C — hydration, cooling, and check-ins prevent heat stroke. B, A, and D invite heat illness.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A family using a faulty space heater reports headache, nausea, and confusion. What should the nurse suspect and advise?
options: Carbon monoxide poisoning; get to fresh air and call emergency services
Stress; ignore it, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Food poisoning; wait it out, at the patient's bedside
The flu; take aspirin, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
explain: Correct: A — headache, nausea, and confusion with fuel-burning heat suggest carbon monoxide; fresh air and emergency care are critical. C, D, and B delay life-saving action.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: A client uses home oxygen. Which safety teaching is correct?
options: Smoke near the oxygen, before the end of the shift
No smoking near oxygen, avoid petroleum-based products, and secure cylinders upright
Store cylinders on their side near heat, as documented in the plan of care
Use petroleum jelly on the nose, then document the patient's response to the intervention
explain: Correct: B — oxygen fuels fire; no smoking, no petroleum products, and secured cylinders prevent disaster. A, D, and C all create fire or injury risk.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which practices are correct when restraints are necessary? Select all that apply.
options: Remove restraints as soon as safely possible
Assess and document the client frequently
Tie restraints to the bed rails
explain: Correct: E, A, C, B — least restrictive first, timely orders, frequent checks, and early removal protect the client. F is abusive. D is unsafe; tie to the bed frame.

q: A client with dementia repeatedly tries to leave the unit. What is the best intervention?
options: Use a wander-guard bracelet, redirect, and engage the client in activities
Ignore the behavior, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Restrain the client permanently, based on the findings documented so far
Lock the client in a room alone, before administering any further medication
explain: Correct: A — wander guards plus redirection keep the client safe with dignity. D is confining. C is excessive. B risks elopement.
domain: Safe and Effective Care: Safety and Infection Control

q: Which are expected findings in a 12-month-old?
options: Reads independently, before the end of the shift
Speaks in full sentences, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
Walks with assistance, says a few words, and uses a pincer grasp
Rides a tricycle, in accordance with facility policy
explain: Correct: C — assisted walking, first words, and pincer grasp fit 12 months. D, B, and A are years ahead.

q: Which signs show a toddler is ready for toilet training? Select all that apply.
options: Stays dry for 2 hours or more
Can pull pants up and down
explain: Correct: C, F, D, B — bladder control, interest, motor skills, and awareness signal readiness. E is arbitrary; readiness varies. A creates power struggles.

q: A school-age child has trouble reading the board. What should the nurse recommend?
options: Move the child permanently to the back row
A vision screening and eye examination
explain: Correct: D — vision screening finds correctable problems early. B delays care. A avoids the issue. C is inappropriate.

q: How should the nurse approach substance use screening with an adolescent?
options: Confidentially and nonjudgmentally, explaining limits of confidentiality
By telling the parents everything immediately, before the end of the shift
By skipping the topic, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
With judgment and threats, on this occasion
explain: Correct: A — private, nonjudgmental screening with clear confidentiality limits gets honest answers. D shuts down disclosure. C misses the risk. B breaks trust.

q: At what age should average-risk colorectal cancer screening begin?
explain: Correct: B — guidelines start screening at 45 for average risk. D and A are too early. C misses a decade of prevention.

q: A 62-year-old postmenopausal client asks about protecting her bones. Which recommendations are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake
Get a DEXA bone density scan as recommended
explain: Correct: C, B, F, E — screening, calcium/vitamin D, loading exercise, and fall prevention protect aging bones. A weakens bone. D causes bone loss.
domain: Health Promotion and Maintenance

q: A pregnant client asks about danger signs. Which should prompt an immediate call to the provider?
options: Mild ankle swelling at the end of the day, as documented in the plan of care
Mild backache, in the form documented in the patient's plan of care
Vaginal bleeding, severe headache, or decreased fetal movement
Occasional heartburn, as it appears in the orders written for this patient
explain: Correct: C — bleeding, severe headache, and reduced movement can signal emergencies. A, D, and B are common discomforts.

q: A postpartum client is rubella-nonimmune. What should the nurse teach?
options: No vaccine is ever needed, before administering any further medication
Get the vaccine during the next pregnancy, under the supervision of the registered nurse
Avoid all vaccines while breastfeeding, on this occasion
Receive the MMR vaccine before discharge and avoid pregnancy for 28 days
explain: Correct: D — vaccinate postpartum before discharge; avoid conception for 28 days. A leaves future pregnancies at risk. B is too late. C is false; MMR is compatible with breastfeeding.

q: The nurse sits quietly with a grieving client without speaking. Which technique is this?

q: Which actions are correct for a client on suicide precautions? Select all that apply.
options: Remove sharp objects and harmful items
Rely only on a no-suicide contract
Recognize that sudden cheerfulness can signal increased risk
Leave the client alone for long periods
explain: Correct: A, E, F, C — remove means, watch closely, build rapport, and know that a sudden lift in mood may mean a plan is set. B alone is unreliable. D removes protection.

q: The family of a client with schizophrenia asks about early warning signs of relapse. What should the nurse teach?
options: Only hallucinations matter, as documented in the plan of care
An improved appetite always signals relapse
Social withdrawal, declining self-care, and unusual thoughts
explain: Correct: D — withdrawal, self-neglect, and odd thinking often precede relapse and should trigger early outreach. C is false. A denies recognizable prodromes. B is too narrow.

q: A client on lithium develops a coarse tremor, confusion, and ataxia. What should the nurse do?
options: Give the next dose as scheduled, in practice
Hold the dose and notify the provider immediately
Discharge the client, at this stage
Encourage more salt, on this occasion, for now
explain: Correct: B — these are lithium toxicity signs; hold the drug and escalate. A worsens toxicity. D is not the treatment. C abandons a toxic client.
domain: Psychosocial Integrity

q: Which interventions are correct during a panic attack? Select all that apply.

q: Two hours into treatment, the glucose is 240 mg/dL and the repeat potassium is 3.4, down from 5.6. Which action is most appropriate?
options: Administer IV potassium as a rapid bolus to correct the level quickly, and assess the patient's understanding of the teaching provided
Notify the provider for potassium replacement — insulin drives potassium into the cells, so potassium must be replaced while the infusion continues
Stop the insulin infusion until the potassium rises above 5.0, and document the findings in the patient's chart
Recheck the potassium in 6 hours with the next scheduled labs, because the patient's condition is considered stable at this time, at the patient's bedside
explain: Correct: B — total-body potassium is depleted in DKA even when the first serum value looks high; insulin and fluids push it down further. At 3.4 the standard action is potassium replacement added to the fluids while insulin continues (insulin is held only when K+ falls below about 3.3). C swings the other way and lets the acidosis rebound. A is never acceptable — IV potassium is never pushed. D waits far too long on a fast-moving value.

q: The provider orders methylergonovine 0.2 mg IM. Which actions are appropriate? Select all that apply.
options: Check the client's blood pressure before administering the medication
Massage the fundus until it is firm while the medication takes effect
Assist the client to void, or catheterize, to empty the bladder
Stop the oxytocin infusion so the two drugs do not conflict
Give the medication by rapid IV push for the fastest effect
explain: Correct: A, B, C — methylergonovine is a vasoconstrictor that can spike blood pressure (and is avoided in hypertension), so the BP is checked first; fundal massage is the immediate mechanical treatment for atony; and an empty bladder lets the uterus contract down instead of being displaced. E is wrong — the order is IM, and IV methylergonovine is reserved for emergencies given slowly with monitoring. D is backwards — oxytocin is first-line therapy and keeps running.
